The return of McLain, a healthy Friedl, and the return of Encarnacion-Strand has me hopeful this time, far different from years past. If this team stays healthy, they can truly compete with the young Pirates team, the Brewers who have lost a lot of talent, and the Cubs who appear to still be adding to their roster. Time will tell and Spring Training will be a good indicator of the roles for each player, as there is competition throughout the entire roster. While a power bat is missing, I think Candelario, Elly, CES, and Hays can provide enough power to put enough runs up on the board for this roster.
Concerns with the Roster
As with any team, there are certainly concerns. A few concerns I have prior to Spring Training include:
· A true power bat is not on this roster.
· Can Lodolo stay healthy?
· If Hunter Greene would get hurt, the rotation could crumble.
· Can Andrew Abbott pitch well after the All-Star break?
· If there are outfield injuries, Cincinnati might require Will Benson, Blake Dunn, Rece Hinds, or Jacob Hurtubise to play more innings than one would like, barring any improvements.
· If Candelario struggles and Marte continues to struggle, will moving roster spots too much with Steer, CES, McLain, and Lux turn into players not getting truly comfortable rather than having defined positions?
Bullpen Preview
In today's game, having a stellar bullpen with depth is much needed in order to provide quality innings. With eight spots to fill, I can only imagine that the bullpen will include the following:
· Graham Ashcraft (Unless he earns a starting role)
· Alexis Diaz
· Emilio Pagan
· Taylor Rogers
· Sam Moll
· Brent Suter
· Up for grabs
· Up for grabs
For the 'up for grabs spots,' Tony Santillan, Carson Spiers, Connor Phillips, Zach Maxwell, Ian Gibaut, Alex Young, and Luis Mey come to mind on potential arms to bolster the pen. I am intrigued about the thought of Ashcraft pitching out of the pen and being able to throw 98-99
mph fastballs and letting loose for a couple innings. He's a high energy guy that I believe would be well suited for a bullpen role.

title: Dominant ‘D' leads Eagles to rout of Chiefs
author: Chuck Hamilton
description: In a game that was seemingly over before it even started, a fierce Philadelphia Eagles defensive front four had its way early and often while obliterating the two-time defending champion Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX. The quartet of Josh Sweat, Milton Williams, Jordan Davis and Jalyx Hunt combined for six sacks of beleaguered Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, and the Eagles soared to a 40-22 win, in a game that felt more like a 50-0 shellacking.
content:
In a game that was seemingly over before it even started, a fierce Philadelphia Eagles defensive front four had its way early and often while obliterating the two-time defending champion Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX. The quartet of Josh Sweat, Milton Williams, Jordan Davis and Jalyx Hunt combined for six sacks of beleaguered Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, and the Eagles soared to a 40-22 win, in a game that felt more like a 50-0 shellacking.
The D-line had plenty of help from their ravenous linebackers and secondary, including a pick-6 from rookie Cooper DeJean on his 22nd birthday. The 38-yard scamper to the end zone gave the green team a 17-0 lead in the second quarter. Philly extended the lead to 24-0 at halftime after linebacker Zack Baun made a diving interception of a Mahomes throw to set up a Jalen Hurts TD toss to A.J. Brown.
Hurts, who took MVP honors after completing 17-of-22 attempts for 221 yards and two scores, along with 72 rushing yards on 11 carries and another TD, was in complete control. Running back Saquon Barkley, who finished with just 57 yards on the ground on 25 carries, was obviously the focus of the Kansas City defense, but Hurts made it appear easy in directing the Eagles to their second-ever Super Bowl title.
Mahomes played one of the worst games of his career, and it was apparent early in the second half that he was going to lead the Chiefs to a miraculous comeback victory. He was able to toss three touchdown passes after the game was already
decided to make the score appear a tad more respectable, but they were essentially meaningless.
It was clear early in this one who the superior team was, and the Eagles could very well emulate KC by winning it all again next year.
*****
IMPROVED 'D' LEADS CATS TO WIN – Speaking of defense, that particular word is one that Kentucky basketball coach Mark Pope is probably sick and tired of hearing. It has been the lack of defense that has been the primary reason for each of the team's seven defeats.
On Saturday afternoon against an admittedly less than average South Carolina team, the Cats showed that they can at the very least play effectively on that end of the court. They played more aggressively and appeared to actually be engaged while attempting to stop the Gamecocks.
After all, isn't that what playing solid defense is all about? Putting forth a concerted effort and demonstrating you possess the 'want to' is what defines playing well defensively. Same goes for rebounding and going after 50-50 balls. For a perfect example, take a look at St. John's and/or Houston. Both of those teams play harassing, in-your-face defense for 40 minutes every single game.
If Pope can inspire this team to even come close to playing that well on the defensive end, there's no telling how deep of a postseason run this group of veteran Cats can make. But that's still conjecture for down the road. The more immediate task is finding a way to finish the regular season on a high note. That is
a tall task indeed in this year's Southeastern Conference minefield.
In yet another case of unfortunate timing for the purposes of this being a timely column, the Kentucky-Tennessee clash was played Tuesday evening, so you will know the result by the time this hits the press. The Volunteers headed into Lexington seeking revenge for the 78-73 loss they suffered to the Cats two weeks prior to last night's game.
The game presents another SEC battle of wills, and the home team will need to keep playing well defensively and not back down from Tennessee. The Vols' defense and physicality are trademarks of how they like to play. Kentucky has shown they can bang as well when needed, with Amari Williams, Otega Oweh and Brandon Garrison providing inside muscle. The trick is to play physical without fouling, while trying to figure out how a particular game will be officiated by the zebras.
The return of point guard Lamont Butler to the starting lineup was a welcome sight to fans Saturday. He looked a bit rusty but having him back leading the team cannot be overstated. His defensive presence and decision-making offensively makes everyone else better, and having him back also means other players can return to positions they're comfortable in, i.e. Jaxson Robinson going back to shooting guard.
The 80-57 win over South Carolina wasn't the most impressive one of the season by any means, but it was important to get back on track after two consecutive defeats. The immediate challenge is keeping that positive momentum going, with a road game looming at Texas on Saturday night, before
returning to Rupp Arena to tangle with Vanderbilt next Wednesday.
*****
ALL YOU NEED IS LOVE – Valentine's Day will be celebrated by many (and ignored by many others) in a couple of days. February 14 is a quasi-holiday that always puts a huge smile on the faces of lots of folks, especially those involved in the greeting card, floral and chocolate industries.
The origin of the day is steeped in legend and speculation. One version says that Saint Valentine of Terni had officiated weddings of Roman soldiers in the 3rd century in secret, against the wishes of Roman Emperor Claudius II, and he was executed on February 14. The same fate befell another martyr by the same name: Valentine. Those romantic anecdotes remain legends, and not necessarily fact.
In 1969, the Roman Catholic Church removed the feast day from its calendar since so little information is known about the martyrs, though St. Valentine is still recognized as a saint.
Centuries later, poet Geoffrey Chaucer linked love with St. Valentine in his 14th century works, and Valentine's Day has been known for love and romance ever since. Other traditions began in the mid-19th century, with men wooing women with flowers and the first heart-shaped box of chocolates being created by Richard Cadbury. By the early 1910s, an American company later known as Hallmark began distributing its more official 'Valentine's Day cards' and now you likely know more than you ever cared to know about February 14.
With the previous history lesson concluded, Happy Valentine's Day to my Valentine, and to all who celebrate!
*****
'It's been a long journey, a journey with ups and downs, highs and lows. You've got to be able to use those experiences that you've had in the past because they're all formative for the future.' – Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts
***** 'When you fish for love, bait with your heart, not your brain.' – Mark Twain

title: MLB teams dream in the spring
author: Chuck Hamilton
description: Despite snowflakes flying and frigid conditions keeping us shivering in our corner of the universe, there are places where the sun is shining and the temperatures are rising.
content:
Despite snowflakes flying and frigid conditions keeping us shivering in our corner of the universe, there are places where the sun is shining and the temperatures are rising.
A couple of those locations include Arizona and Florida, where 30 Major League Baseball teams are preparing for the upcoming grind of the 162-game regular season. Teams not named the White Sox, Athletics, Marlins, and Rockies, are looking ahead to the season with varied levels of hope, anticipation and optimism. Fans of the aforementioned quartet have no realistic expectations of contending for anything but the cellar in their respective divisions.
That leaves 26 other franchises with some hope, even though the majority will fall woefully short of reaching the postseason. There are the obvious favorites, also known as the big spenders, teams like the Dodgers, Yankees, Phillies, Braves, Mets and Padres.
There is a larger group of teams with reasonable expectations and certainly capable of making a legitimate run at either winning their division or earning a Wild Card spot. Those teams include the Orioles, Red Sox, Royals, Tigers, Guardians, Mariners, Diamondbacks, Brewers and Cubs. Several other teams are looking to bounce back from disappointing 2024 campaigns, including the Rangers, Blue Jays, Rays, Twins, Angels, Cardinals, Reds, Pirates, Giants and Nationals.
There are undoubtedly some folks who believe with all their heart that their team can or will be playing in October, no matter how awful they appear to be on paper, and you cannot
tell them otherwise. Not in the spring anyway. That's because this is the time of year that is filled with hundreds of well-worn clichés, with the most infamous one being 'hope springs eternal.' As we've mentioned before however, clichés only become clichés because there is a lot of truth to them.
*****
REDS HAVE REAL SHOT AT CONTENDING — There is definitely an air of eager anticipation in Goodyear, Ariz. That's where the Cincinnati Reds are preparing for what some observers and fans are convinced will be a winning season after last year's less than mediocre 77-85 record.
There are several reasons for the optimism, but there are also several questions yet to be answered in the spring. One of the primary points for hope is that the Reds can compete in the perception that the National League Central, which is not exactly stacked with teams that strike fear into anybody.
Defending division champion Milwaukee ran away from the rest of the division a year ago, but several key pieces have departed, while the Cubs appeared to have strengthened themselves during the offseason. The Cardinals seem to be in a rebuild phase, but they could still be a contender in a weak division. The Pirates began last year like they were going to contend before reverting back to being the Pirates.
The NL Central is up for grabs in 2025, and if the Reds can avoid serious injuries to their starting pitchers and their most productive hitters, they have a shot. It seems inconceivable, but the Reds used 16 different starting pitchers in 2024, and that is no recipe for success. The entire starting staff spent time on the injured list, and the hope is that the addition of Brady Singer
and an improved bullpen will be an area of strength. Keeping the staff relatively healthy will be the key. If that can be accomplished, and the lineup produces to its potential, the Reds should at least compete for a Wild Card, if not win the division. New manager Terry Francona is also looking at improving a couple of other areas – defense and baserunning — that were disastrous at times last season.
It remains debatable just how much of a difference a manager can make, but Francona appears to be the right man for the job at the right time. The players are already impressed and fired up to play for the future Hall of Fame skipper, with veteran reliever Brent Suter saying that his talk that greeted the team on Monday to begin spring training was the best baseball speech he has ever heard.
There should be a noticeable difference on and off the field, with the Reds playing with more focus and enthusiasm than the team we got accustomed to watching the past couple of years. Whether or not it is enough to contend is why they play the games. We can analyze the roster, possible lineup combinations, and the pitching staff ad infinitum, but if the players don't perform on the field, it won't matter who is making out the lineup card.
*****
'Spring training means flowers, people coming outdoors, sunshine, optimism and baseball. Spring training is a time to think about being young again.' — Ernie Banks
*****
'Well enough for old folks to rise early, because they have done so many mean things all their lives they can't sleep anyhow.' – Mark Twain

title: Bracken wins their third
description: The Bracken County Lady Bears and Mason County Lady Royals tipped off at the Fieldhouse Thursday evening for the 39th district girls' basketball championship.
content:
The Bracken County Lady Bears and Mason County Lady Royals tipped off at the Fieldhouse Thursday evening for the 39th district girls' basketball championship.
Throughout the regular season, the Lady Bears and Lady Royals saw one another twice, with Mason County taking both contests. The first, a 57-47 win at Bracken County's home gym, and the second a 61-55 win at the Fieldhouse. After defeating Augusta 62-46 in the 39th district semifinals, the Lady Bears were eager to take on the Lady Royals once again for a shot at their third straight district championship.
Mason County, having fallen to the Lady Bears in last year's championship round, were looking for redemption, and hoping to bring in yet another win over Bracken County.
When the two teams took to the floor of the Fieldhouse, both were fighting to establish an early lead. By the end of the first eight minutes of play, it was Bracken County that had pulled ahead, leading 17-8 over the Lady Royals. Off to a slow start, the Lady Royals hoped to regroup heading into the second quarter, and close the nine point deficit before heading into halftime.
'Our defense is something we've really been working on. That's something that these girls pride themselves on is their defense, we finally got them to buy in that defense is what wins games. Defense will create your offense, if you can be patient on offense, and I think we did a great job of being patient, I don't think we forced too many.' said Lady Bears head coach, Troy Archibald.
Bracken County's defense continued to hold off the Lady Royals throughout the second quarter, holding Mason County to just 12. In the second, the Lady Bears continued to work on the offensive end, putting up eight more than Mason County for a 37-20 lead heading into halftime.
'We've played good basketball for a while, and I told the kids we picked a really bad time to have a bad first half. That's one of the worst halves of the year that we've had. We've had a couple games this year where we've dug some holes, but we just couldn't get defensive stops.' said Lady Royals head coach, Jay Fite.
Down 17 at the half, the Lady Royals knew they needed to return to the court refocused, and slow down the Bracken County offense. The Lady Bears hoped to maintain their lead throughout the remainder of the contest, with their strong defense aiming to hold back Mason County's top shooters like Amirah Reed and Lexi Young.
Upon returning to the court in the third, Bracken County jumped out ahead of the Lady Royals yet again, but Mason County stayed in the fight and were able to outscore the Lady Bears 13-12. Midway through the quarter, Reed knocked down one of three three-point goals scored this contest, crossing the thousand career point mark.
'Congratulations to Amirah Reed getting to a thousand points, and she's not done by any means.' said coach Archibald.
Although Mason County were able to outscore the Lady Bears this quarter, Bracken County still had a 16 point lead heading into the final eight minutes of play, leading 49-33 over Mason County.
'They've got some really good players and we were gonna have to leave and go double, and trap. They see the floor really well, and they share the ball really well. If we didn't turn them over, they made us pay for those and they got some finishes on the backside or got to the free throw line. We tried several different things pressure wise, but if we were in man, we were struggling to stay in front, if we went zone, we struggled to find the shooters. A lot of aspects just weren't in our favor tonight.' said coach Fite.
Mason County once again outscored the Lady Bears by one point in the fourth, putting up 15 this quarter. Although putting up two less points than the Lady Royals in the second half, Bracken County was able to maintain the lead they had built in the first half, and roll through to a 63-48 victory over Mason County, bringing home their third straight 39th district championship.
'Three straight, man, it's an unbelievable feeling. These girls, they just give it everything they've got every time they step out on the floor.' said coach Archibald, 'We've worked on Mason County pretty much all season, what we were gonna do if we were fortunate enough to see them in the finals. Defensively, what we worked on, it worked. We executed defensively, and we let our defense dictate our offense. When you can handle Mason County's pressure, good things are gonna happen. They're a solid team, great players and coach Fite does an excellent job.'
Following this contest, both teams will now move on to continue competing in the 10th region girls' basketball tournament at Campbell County Middle School next week.
'That's what we told them, as tough as it was this evening, we're still playing basketball. We've gotta find a way to pick ourselves up and see what the draw holds for us tomorrow morning, and take a couple days to prep, plan, and hopefully come out with a lot more energy than we did in the first half tonight.' said coach Fite.
The Lady Royals will take on the George Rogers Clark Lady Cardinals in the first round of the 10th region girls' basketball tournament on Monday, with the contest scheduled to tip off at 7:45 p.m. Bracken County's next contest will be against the Harrison County Fillies in the 10th region quarterfinals, scheduled to tip off at 6:00 p.m. on Tuesday.
LADY BEARS 17-20-12-14 – 63
LADY ROYALS 8-12-13-15 – 48

Field Goals: Bracken 16, Mason 12
Three-Pointers: Bracken 6, Mason 6
Free throws: Bracken 15/21, Mason 6/12
Records: Bracken 22-10, Mason 21-9
