title: Missing Maysville woman found deceased
description: Eugenia Harris Cooley of Maysville who has been missing since mid Dec. has been found deceased…
content:
Eugenia Harris Cooley of Maysville who has been missing since mid Dec. has been found deceased,
The Maysville Police Department released a statement around 2 p.m. that their department and officials with the Buffalo Trace Search and Rescue located her body near the area of Wald Park which is in Mason County.
MPD representatives stated that they are working with the Mason County Coroner's Office and the State Medical Examiners Office to ascertain more information. Few details have been released at this time as it is an ongoing investigation.
'The Maysville Police Department would like to thank all of those who assisted in search efforts including Buffalo Trace Search and Rescue, Mason County Sheriff's Office, Mason County Emergency Management, Anderson Township Fire Department, Hamilton County Police Association Underwater Search and Recovery Unit, and the community at large.'
Cooley was reported missing on New Year's Day and was last seen on or around Dec. 20-21.
At the time she was reported missing Det. Ryan Hull had stated that some of her belongings had been found in a garbage receptacle near her residence.
'It looks like she had put some of her personal property in a garbage can right outside of her apartment which, you know, it sounds bad but we still don't know,' stated Hull.
Hull had noted that there were no leads at that time.
He indicated that they had no reason to believe that her disappearance was in any way connected to mental illness or substance abuse.
'Nobody is saying that she had any kind of mental health issues or early onset Alzheimer's or anything like that or blood sugar issue that would cause a mental issue. Also as far as we can find she had no drug issues of anything like that,' remarked Hull.
Hull added that he had called multiple services attempting to get information on her whereabouts.
'I've called every hospital, ambulance service, taxi service, everything like that to see if we can get a time frame on her but nothing so far,' Hull explained.
This investigation is ongoing. Additional information will be released as it is given.

title: Will the Cats flog the Hogs?
author: Chuck Hamilton
description: Before I offer my opinions on the huge showdown in Rupp Arena this evening, I have a confession or two to impart.
content:
Before I offer my opinions on the huge showdown in Rupp Arena this evening, I have a confession or two to impart.
I was wrong.
I know, shocking, right?
It was far from the first time, and it is also far from the last time. In my most recent column, I didn't give Kentucky much of a chance of winning in Knoxville on Tuesday evening. After all, the Cats were playing shorthanded, the Vols were coming off a tough road loss at Auburn, and they were overdue for a good performance against their border rivals.
Coach Mark Pope and his gritty bunch had other ideas.
Despite the absence of starting point guard and team catalyst Lamont Butler, along with 6-foot-11 forward Andrew Carr (who tried to give it a go but to no avail), others stepped up and in a big way.
Koby Brea broke out of his recent shooting slump and didn't miss a shot from the floor at Tennessee. He led the way with 18 points on 5-for-5 from the field, which included three from beyond the arc. Jaxson Robinson showed his steadiness, dropping in 17 points, including four critical 3-pointers.
Otega Oweh, the most physical presence on the roster, tallied 14 points and grabbed six boards, and 'point center' Amari Williams, who still drives me crazy at times, played an excellent floor game with a double-double that included 10 points and a game-high 15 rebounds to go with a team-high four assists. Ansley Almonor, starting in place of Carr, continued his hot shooting from behind the arc, connecting on four bombs for his
12-point contribution. Freshman Trent Noah stepped up as well, coming off the bench to drain a timely three and add a total of five points to the effort.
Kentucky's 78-point output was the most points allowed by the vaunted UT defense this season, and the Cats were able to withstand repeated comeback attempts by the orange team in front of the 22,272 patrons inside Food City Arena. A huge factor in the upset victory – UK was a 10-point underdog – was an overall shooting percentage of 50 percent from the field, as well as the 3-point line, where the Cats sank 12-of-24 attempts. Meanwhile, the Vols missed 34 of their 45 long-range attempts – many were wide-open looks — with point guard Zakai Zeigler making just one of his 11 tries.
Any win in the Southeastern Conference this season is a welcome sight, and when you can steal one on the road, that makes it even sweeter. Being wrong isn't the worst thing in the world, and this time, I'm glad I was wrong. My observations in this space are simply my opinions, and admittedly I'm unabashedly a fan of certain teams. I make the best attempt I can to simply tell it the way I see it, and present an objective viewpoint, and I'm usually even more critical of the teams I pull for.
One more opinion (gripe?) concerning college basketball before I get to the Arkansas-Kentucky clash this evening:
The powers-that-be need to take a look at the excessive reviews that take place, especially near the end of games. I understand you want to get the call correct if possible, but there are numerous calls made throughout every game that are questionable, to say the least. Many of the trips made to the
monitor take far too long, making the game much longer than it should be. As my son Chris aptly and succinctly describes the reviews and officials in general, the game becomes a 'ref show' and detracts from the flow, thereby decreasing the enjoyment of watching college hoops.
*****
TO BOO OR NOT TO BOO? – OK, now it's time to weigh in on the hot topic surrounding this evening's return to Rupp Arena from a certain former UK coach.
I'm not telling ticket-buyers what to do when John Calipari leads his Arkansas Razorbacks, but they have the right to do as they please, within reason, of course. The reception will likely be mixture of cheers and boos, and he deserves both. Cheers for what he did during his first 10 years in Lexington, and boos for the last five, especially the disappointing and unacceptable early exits in March to lesser foes.
It wasn't just the painful losses to inferior opponents that got under the skin of close followers of the program, but rather some of the things he uttered to diehard Kentucky fans. They felt like Cal was condescending and arrogant, labeling them as 'basketball bennies', inferring that he knows more about the game than the fans, while stubbornly refusing to make any changes to his outdated philosophy.
All of that is history now, but none of it is forgotten, and the highly-anticipated matchup is here at last. After all, numerous UK fans have had this one circled on their calendars since the schedule was released. So, what will happen after the game tips off? I don't know for certain; after all, if I had a crystal ball, I would use it to play the lottery.
My best guess is that the struggling Razorbacks, led by former Cat Adou Thiero, will play with the most intensity that have played with all season. It will also be interesting to see how well the other ex-Wildcats, Zvonimir Ivisic and D.J. Wagner, perform in their return to Rupp.
Look for the Hogs to try to crash the offensive glass, and play a physical style in an effort to replicate what Georgia and others have done against Kentucky this season. The Thiero-Oweh matchup should be a fun one to watch, and without Butler's defensive presence at the point, Wagner could be tough to stop with his ability to penetrate to the hoop and his ability to dish to open shooters on the perimeter.
The Cats present matchup problems for Arkansas as well, and it says here that as long as UK is making threes, handling the glass effectively, and keeping turnovers to a minimum, they will prevail. The stress level for Kentucky fans will be through the roof, and if the Cats can avoid any prolonged scoring droughts and play with intensity on the defensive end, the roof could be blown off the place.
The game represents added importance in the SEC race; UK can ill afford another home conference loss if it has designs on finishing in the top four of the league, and earn a bye in what will be a highly competitive tournament in Nashville's Bridgestone Arena, beginning on March 12.
Against my better judgment, let's say: Kentucky 84, Arkansas 73.
*****
REDS MAKING POSITIVE MOVES – The Cincinnati Reds appear to actually be going for it in 2025. Despite not signing any high-
priced free agents, the club has added several key pieces to a team that has the potential to at least claim a National League Central Division title.
The biggest acquisition of them all has to be the guy who will be wearing the rare number 77 in the dugout. That would be new skipper and proven winner Terry Francona, who is expected to change the team's culture, and hopefully, win a lot more games that last season.
'Tito' will also have more to work with that former manager David Bell, as long as the key pieces can remain healthy. The starting rotation features a solid combination of talent and youth, and former Kansas City Royal Brady Singer should fit in nicely. The bullpen has been upgraded in recent days as well, with the addition of former University of Kentucky lefty Taylor Rogers being acquired from the San Francisco Giants. The 34-year-old had a 2.40 ERA and fanned 64 in 60 innings last season.
The addition of backup catcher Jose Trevino gives the Reds a solid option defensively while affording starting receiver Tyler Stephenson some needed off days from his duties behind the plate.
Infielder Gavin Lux, who came over from the world champion LA Dodgers, was an interesting pickup, and gives the club even more versatility. Just this past week, the Reds signed outfielder Austin Hays to a $5 million deal, giving the team a possible low-risk, high-reward return. It will be interesting to see if Hays bounces back from a 2024 season where he suffered a serious kidney infection, and returns to his 2023 form, when he was
named an American League All-Star while playing for the Baltimore Orioles.
Another signing that could pay off occurred a few days ago when the club announced veteran lefty Wade Miley agreed to a minor-league deal. Miley is on the mend from Tommy John surgery and is aiming for a return to the mound in late May. Even if he doesn't make it back to the big-league club, Miley should be a positive influence on the young pitchers in Louisville.
While writing this blurb on this gloomy Friday morning, a report from Jon Heyman of the New York Post says that the Reds are interested in signing power-hitting Mets first baseman Pete Alonso to a free-agent deal. Heyman admitted 'it's probably a long shot' but if the usual penny-pinching ownership pulls it off, the Cincy lineup would suddenly be a force to be reckoned with.
*****
'I don't know if I have a lot of comments on it. I love the drama. I think it's Kentucky, right? It follows us and everything we do. It's one of the beautiful things about getting to coach here and play here, be associated with this program, is we care.' – Mark Pope, when asked about the national attention being heaped upon the UK-Arkansas game
*****
'Death, the only immortal who treats us all alike, whose pity and whose peace and whose refuge are for all – the soiled and the pure, the rich and the poor, the loved and the unloved.' — Mark Twain

title: KSP identifies body discovered in the Ohio River
description: A body was discovered in the Ohio River near Dover.
content:
A body was discovered in the Ohio River near Dover.
According to Mason County Sheriff Ryan Swolsky, a body was located by boat in the Ohio River in the vicinity of Dover on Monday, Feb.3 at 9:30 a.m.
Sheriff's Office personnel were joined by the Maysville Fire Department, Mason County Coroner, the Maysville Police Department, and Kentucky State Police at the scene where the body was recovered and identified.
Swolsky stated that no foul play is suspected but the case is under investigation.
KSP identified the deceased individual as David Blevins Jr., 47, of Staffordsville, Ky.
Blevins had been reported as missing by the Johnson County Sheriff's Office in Dec. of 2024 according to KSP.
KSP is officially working on the investigation with assistance from the Mason County Sheriff's Office.
More information will be shared once it is released.

title: Day 25: Tanji Shivener
description: The Ledger Independent is publishing a 50/50 series featuring 50 things over 50 weeks. During this series, our readers can expect to see different 'Local Talents/Artisans' each week.
content:
The Ledger Independent is publishing a 50/50 series featuring 50 things over 50 weeks. During this series, our readers can expect to see different 'Local Talents/Artisans' each week.
Some of the 'Local Talents/Artisans' that may be featured will include artists, authors, songwriters and more. The general definition of 'artisan' refers to a worker in a skilled trade, according to the Oxford Dictionary.
Please enjoy Day 25 of the series.
Mason County resident Tanji Shivener is a published novelist who grew up in Brown County, Ohio.
Shivener wrote her first of 10 novels in 2019.
'My husband suggested I do something for myself as I am always doing and taking care of others as a nurse,' explained Shivener. 'I wrote 1,700 words in the notes app of my phone — the beginning of my first novel — Ginger Devil. I ended up buying a laptop the next day and continued to write the story.'
Her first novel, Ginger Devil, was published in 2020.
Shivener stated that she developed a love for reading after being given an assignment as a seventh grader to read The Giver.
'I realized some books were actually interesting to me. As an adolescent, I found that the majority of required reading in grade school was almost dreadful. After I discovered pleasure in reading, I read as many novels as I could get my hands on,' stated Shivener.
She further stated that she never actually intended to become a writer.
'I never actually dreamt of being a writer or an author, but I've always had stories in my head, and being a storyteller has seemed to come naturally to me,' she noted.
Shivener stated that her talent gives her a feeling of achievement that 'even a little girl from the trailer park can grow up to be a novelist'.
Shivener loves to connect with her readers.
'A person can learn more about me and my talents from my social media (I have Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok — although I don't claim to know how to use them very well).'
Shiveners books can be purchased online at Amazon, Barnes and Noble, or can be checked out at public libraries. Signed copies of her book can be purchased at Local Ky 68. She also has a website: tmshivener.com.
Shivener, who writes under the name of T.M. Shivener, has a series called The Trailer Park series which is suggested for ages 14 and up.
She has a plethora of stand-alone romance books suggested for ages 18 and up; Ginger Devil, Thirty, Flirty, and Dumb, Why It's Called a Goodbye, Bad Seed, Sihn and Ruin in River Falls, and Paint Splattered Teardrops which is set to be released in Winter 2025.
Shiveners Psycological Thrillers are also suggested for ages 18 and up and consist of a duo of books; She Is Me, Too, and She is Within Me. A stand-alone thriller titled Forever Twenty-Nine is set to come out in May 2025.
Shivener has a book signing scheduled for Saturday, Feb. 22 at Barn Chick's Coffee Shop beginning at 1 p.m. located in Ripley, Ohio and at Hemingway's in Maysville on March 15 from noon to 2 p.m.

title: Fleming County '2-0' after defeating West Carter
description: The Fleming County Panthers hosted the West Carter Comets on the basketball court Thursday night.
content:
The Fleming County Panthers hosted the West Carter Comets on the basketball court Thursday night.
As the 2024-25 regular basketball season winds down, and teams play their last games of the year before tipping off in district tournaments, each one remaining on the schedule serves as preparation for postseason. Which is exactly how the Fleming County Panthers viewed their Thursday night contest with the Comets.
Prior to the contest, Fleming County senior Seth Hickerson was honored as the Panthers' all time leading scorer, with a total of 2,222 career points before tipping off against the Comets.
A fellow 16th region team, the Comets entered the contest 4-21 on the season, hoping to pick up some wins late in the season. Fleming County sat at 17-10, three spots back from the top team in the 16th region, according to RPI.
Once the contest got underway, scoring was slow in the first few minutes. Neither team was able to score a basket in the first two minutes of play, but it was Fleming County that got the first few points on the board. As the first quarter continued, the Panthers picked up an early solid lead over the Comets, outscoring them 21-11 by the end of the first eight minutes.
'I thought we executed very well. We shot a very high percentage from the three and the two, only disappointment was the free throws. We were only 54 percent there, last night we were 88 percent against Nicholas. I was very pleased with the way we shot the ball, from behind the arc and inside. Our execution was pretty good, and everybody shared the ball. We had 22 assists on 30 made field goals, that's excellent.' said Panthers head coach, James Biggs.
Up 10 heading into the second quarter, Fleming County looked to continue furthering their lead over West Carter to close out the first half of play.
Throughout the remainder of the first half, the Panthers' offense continued to score, but it was the defense that kept things under control during the second quarter. Fleming County held West Carter to just eight points this quarter, outscoring them by seven to lead 39-19 heading into halftime.
'I thought other than the third quarter I thought our defense was kinda dominant. Held them to 11 in the first, eight in the second and nine in the fourth. I was very pleased. Anytime you hold a varsity basketball team to under 50 points you should win and I thought our defense was for the most part spot on.' said coach Biggs, 'Rebounding we got beat by one tonight on the glass, that's a little disappointing but I thought our first shot defense was excellent for the most part.'
Returning to the court after halftime, the Panthers hoped to once again remain on top offensively, and continue holding off the West Carter shooters. The Comets however, refused to quit and made the third quarter their biggest of the night.
Outscoring the Panthers 19-14 in the third, West Carter did their best to fight their way back into the contest in the second half, but were still down 15 heading into the fourth quarter, Fleming County leading 53-38. After a slow third quarter, the Panthers were looking to regain control of the contest in the final few minutes of play, and lock down the defensive end once again.
In the fourth, Fleming County was once again able to hold off the Comets' offense, allowing just nine points to West Carter, while the offense put up 26 more, leading 79-47 when the final buzzer sounded.
'I feel good. It's been a long three weeks here, we've played 12 games in the last whatever, 18, 19 days. Four, four and three in a row this week, so, it's been a long stretch. We've had some ups and downs, we've played some really elite competition. Took some lumps, but now we're back on a two game winning streak here at home. We'll take some time off and then we've got a really good Augusta team coming here on Tuesday, and then obviously the district tournament's right around the corner so we're looking forward and prepping for that already.' said coach Biggs.
On Tuesday, the Fleming County Panthers will host the Augsuta Panthers in what will be their second to last regular season game of the year, before heading to Lewis County to take on the Lions on Thursday. Fleming County will then make sure they're prepped and ready for the 61st district tournament as postseason play gets underway.
'I feel good about it. You can see the light at the end of the tunnel here, we're getting excited because we know once you get to that point it's win or go home. We've played a brutal schedule all year long, and we're still sitting here at 18-10. We've maybe let a few slip away that we shouldn't have, but our record is what it is and it can't change. All we can do is improve from here.' said coach Biggs, 'We went in to our meeting Wednesday before we played Nicholas after Boyd beat us and just said look, we're 0-0, we wanna be 6-0 at the end of this six game stretch, which would put us as district champions and headed to Morehead 22-10.'

title: Coach Adams ready to take charge of the Royals
description: A press conference was held Friday, Feb. 14 at the Mason County Fieldhouse to welcome new head Mason County football coach, Tony Adams.
content:
A press conference was held Friday, Feb. 14 at the Mason County Fieldhouse to welcome new head Mason County football coach, Tony Adams.
With the departure of coach Joe Wynn at the end of the 2024 football season, the Royals are excited to compete in 2025 under coach Adams. The Mason County football team has seen plenty of success in recent years, and coach Adams is eager to continue bringing in wins on the gridiron for Mason County.
'This is a new and exciting chapter, and I'm ready to embrace the responsibility of leading the Royals to success. Being a member of Mason County High School is a privilege. My family and I are thankful for this opportunity.' said coach Adams.
As the defensive coordinator and linebackers coach, coach Adams helped lead the Greenwood Gators to a second round Class 5A playoff appearance in 2022, going 9-3 that season. The following year, the Gators saw a first round playoff appearance, falling to the Graves County Eagles. As the defensive coordinator his last season with the Gators, Adams helped his team's defense pick up 580 total tackles, 27 tackles for loss and six sacks.
Coach Adams attended Greenwood High School where he played football for legendary high school coach Ed Smart. Adams received a Bachelor's Degree in Business Management from Mid-Continent University in 2006 and his Master's in Teaching LBD in K-12 Special Education in 2022 from the University of The Cumberlands. Coach Adams has been married for 21 years to his wife Valerie and together they have 3 children: Tyler, Aden and Adysen.
Now the head coach of the Mason County Royals, Adams is eager to help Mason County return to the playoffs in 2025, and advance well into the 2025 class 4A postseason.
'I think playing at Bowling Green and South Warren every year for the last five years and then even before that, they've got kids that are going D-1, all over the country. So, I've learned how to plan for teams like that, how to get kids ready for teams like that, because you have to be simple, you have to be precise and you have to do the little things really well and that's what has prepared me for that.' said coach Adams.
Mason County's primary goals when they take the football field in 2025 are the same as they've always been, with a few additions. Defeat the Bracken County Polar Bears, continue their four game win streak over the Fleming County Panthers, defeat the Covington Catholic Colonels, and win the state championship.
Coach Adams, and the rest of the Royals are excited to get the next season underway, and are anxiously counting down the days before they can return to the field to practice.

title: Missing person located after extensive search
description: A woman has been located after being reported missing this week in Maysville.
content:
A woman has been located after being reported missing this week in Maysville.
The Maysville Police Department stated on Tuesday, Feb. 18 that it was investigating a missing person, Tammy Woods Carpenter.
MPD noted that Carpenter had last been seen on Wednesday, Feb. 12 in the area of 303 River Drive and was last seen wearing a shirt with a red design and white or tan sweatpants.
This evening on Wednesday, Feb. 19, MPD stated that it conducted an extensive search with members from the Buffalo Trace Search and Rescue Team and Mason County Emergency Management Director in an area behind the Mason County Animal Rescue Shelter.
'During the investigation, video was located which placed the missing female around the animal shelter on Feb. 12 at approximately 7:20 a.m. walking north towards the empty field and the Ohio River,' MPD said.
It was around 3:45 p.m. on Feb. 19 that Carpenter was located by the search team and was found deceased 'in a wooded area on the edge of the open field, close to the backwaters of the Ohio River,' MPD expressed.
'Officers contacted the Mason County Corner as well as the Maysville Fire Department to assist in the recovery of the deceased female,' MPD stated.
MPD further noted that Carpenter would be taken to have an autopsy conducted by the State Medical Examiner and that the investigation would remain ongoing until the completion of it.
'The Maysville Police Department would like to thank all the callers who provided information regarding Ms. Carpenter's disappearance. We exhausted every lead that came into us. This is a tragic event that takes an enormous toll on our community. At this time in the investigation, no foul play is suspected, pending autopsy reports,' MPD stated.

title: Lady Royals advance to district championship
description: In the first of two 39th district girls' semifinal matchups on Monday, the Mason County Lady Royals took on the St. Pat Lady Saints at the Fieldhouse.
content:
In the first of two 39th district girls' semifinal matchups on Monday, the Mason County Lady Royals took on the St. Pat Lady Saints at the Fieldhouse.
Throughout the season, the Lady Royals and Lady Saints saw each other twice in a pair of district tournament seeding contests. Both times, the Lady Royals came out on top, with a pair of decisive victories. Despite this, St. Pat has spent the season preparing for the postseason and gradually improving throughout the year, in hopes of being a contender when the district tournament arrived.
When the game tipped off Monday evening, both teams took to the floor hoping to advance to tomorrow's 39th district championship contest. St. Pat fought hard throughout the first eight minutes of play, but it was Mason County standing tall with an 18-10 lead heading into the second quarter.
'The girls put in a lot of work, and everybody got better every day. That showed tonight and we'll just continue to get better in the future.' said Lady Saints head coach, Isaac Klee.
With an eight point lead heading into the second quarter, Mason County hoped to build upon it heading into halftime, while the Lady Saints looked to battle back and close the point deficit. The Lady Royals defense however would hold St. Pat to just three points in the second, while the Lady Royals put up 21 more on the offensive end, for a 39-13 lead heading into halftime.
'I think we came out of the gates a little flat, I think St. Pat had a lot of good energy early, we came out a little flat and a little timid actually. Then we finally loosened up a little bit and became the aggressors. That's the way we normally start the game and we wanna make sure we continue doing that moving forward.' said Lady Royals head coach, Jay Fite.
Upon returning to the court after halftime, the Lady Royals continued to work hard on both ends of the court. In the third, Mason County held St. Pat to just two points, outscoring them by 15 for a 56-15 lead heading into the final few minutes of the contest.
'I thought we did a good job finding Lexi early, she made some nice moves inside, got to the rim and also got to the free throw line to kinda get things going for us. Amirah did a good job of finding some other people, driving the gaps and finding some other people for some open looks, she wasn't as aggressive for herself offensively, but she was finding open people as well.' said coach Fite.
In the fourth, St. Pat would finally outscore Mason County, putting up 10 points on the offensive end, while the Lady Royals slowed down to just seven. Unfortunately for the Lady Saints, Mason County had built up a large lead, and would take the contest 63-25 at the end of the fourth quarter, putting an end to St. Pat's 2024-25 season.
'I feel good, we improved every time, we improved that time. Score wise and effort wise, we gave everything we had. They're a great team, they're the number one seed for a reason, and it'll be a good matchup for who ever faces them in the finals.' said coach Klee, 'Our four seniors, Caroline Poczatek, Emma Gallenstein, Allie Cascio and Kahdyn Kimball, gave a lot of time effort and energy. Emma finishes with a career 500 rebounds and that's gonna be hard to replace, but we'll be alright.'
With this win the Lady Royals now move on to the 39th district girls' championship game scheduled for tomorrow evening at 6:00 p.m. at the Fieldhouse. Mason County will take on the winners of the second semifinal round contest between the Bracken County Lady Bears and Augusta Lady Panthers, and will be prepared for either opponent when game time arrives.
'We're gonna sit here and watch this game and find out who we're gonna play, and we're gonna definitely make sure we're prepping for it. We're fortunate to have a couple days to prep and get ready. We have played both teams twice, so obviously we have gotten a feel for them. So, whoever it is, we just gotta make sure we're ready to come out, be the aggressors, have some early energy and be ready to play for the entire game, because both those teams are gonna bring it.' said coach Fite.

title: Augusta puts up strong fight, Bracken County advances to the championship
description: In the first round of the 2025 39th district girls' basketball tournament, the Bracken County Lady Bears took on the Augusta Lady Panthers at the Mason County Fieldhouse Monday night.
content:
In the first round of the 2025 39th district girls' basketball tournament, the Bracken County Lady Bears took on the Augusta Lady Panthers at the Mason County Fieldhouse Monday night.
The two teams had become very familiar with one another throughout the regular season, with the district moving to seeding at the start of 2024-25. The Lady Bears and Lady Panthers saw each other twice in the regular season, Bracken County coming away with a pair of wins over Augusta, entering the tournament 4-2 against district opponents. Augusta, despite the two prior losses to the Lady Bears were eager to compete when they took the floor of the Fieldhouse, hoping for an upset victory and a shot at their first ever 39th district title, while the Lady Bears hoped to advance and bring home their third straight.
At tipoff, the Lady Panthers came out of the gate strong in the first quarter, putting up the first points and going on a run that would provide Augusta with a 26-12 lead at the end of the first eight minutes of play.
'For years, I was an assistant coach under Jason Hinson on the boys side, and one thing he taught me about the postseason is, the first five minutes of a postseason game are the most important. Especially when you're the underdog, you've gotta come out and you've gotta punch the other team in the mouth so to speak, and we did that. You've gotta be able to make shots, and we made shots in the first quarter. That kept us in the game for a long time.' said Lady Panthers head coach, Todd Kelsch.
Unfortunately for the Lady Panthers, their 14 point lead heading into the second quarter would be short lived, with the Lady Bears making an adjustment on the defensive end, and marking a strong offensive comeback.
As the first half continued, Bracken County would hold Augusta to just three points in the second quarter, outscoring them by 19, to head into halftime up 34-29.
'We just knew we had to keep the ball pressure up. Our defense has what's been really helping us here lately. The girls have really bought into what we're trying to do defensively, they're rotating, they're helping one another a lot more now than what they used to, we're more patient with the basketball, we'll move the ball a lot better and then we finally get an open look underneath. Things are improving defensively and offensively, and that's what we gotta continue to do.' said Lady Bears head coach, Troy Archibald.
After falling behind in the first quarter, and working their way back into the lead by halftime, the Lady Bears were ready to go when they returned to the court after halftime, while the Lady Panthers had proved to themselves they could compete, and were looking to close the five point deficit and get back out ahead late in the contest.
Throughout the third, both teams were relatively evenly matched, Bracken County putting up two more points than the Lady Panthers for a seven point, 46-39 lead heading into the fourth and final quarter of the game. Although down seven points, Augusta refused to quit, and were hoping for a strong offensive performance in the last eight minutes of the contest.
'That's kinda what we wanted to do was to stay within two possessions to really give us a chance toward the end, we just gave so much in that third quarter we kinda ran out of gas toward the end to really pull us closer. All in all, I'm super proud of our team.' said coach Kelsch.
Bracken County cemented their lead in the fourth, putting up 16 more while holding the Lady Panthers to just seven, ending the contest up 62-48. Despite a continuous effort from the Augusta offense, the Lady Panthers just couldn't close the gap, this loss putting an end to their 2024-25 season.
'We had three seniors this year, and what I said to our underclassmen was, learn from these three girls because they all had different roles on the team, and they were stars in their role. Reagan got a lot of attention from everybody because she was our scorer, Kenzington, she was a vocal leader, and then Mallory started as our manager last year and this summer we only had eight or nine showing up to practices. I begged her to join the team and she joined so that we would have five on five in practice. I owe a lot to those girls.' said coach Kelsch.
With this win, the Lady Bears now move on to the district championship tomorrow evening, where they will face off against the Mason County Lady Royals, both teams just as hungry for a district championship win as the other.
'Yeah, we've played them twice, they got us both times. It was close, ten points the first time, six points the second game up here. There's just some things defensively we need to work on, and I think where we are defensively right now we'll be in a good spot to win that game. Regardless of who wins it, it's gonna be a fun game to watch. The crowd is gonna see two teams play their hearts out, and it's gonna be under 10 either way I think.' said coach Archibald, 'Coach Fite's done a fantastic job with those girls. Amirah, Lexi, Buttery, Hughes, Perry all of them can shoot the ball, they get up and down the floor and they're gonna pressure us, so we've just gotta stay composed and handle that pressure and I think we'll be ok.'
The 39th district girls' championship game will be held at the Mason County Fieldhouse tomorrow evening, scheduled for a 6:00 p.m. tipoff.

title: Mason County secures number nine
description: The Mason County Royals and Augusta Panthers took to the floor of the Fieldhouse Thursday evening for the 39th district boys' basketball championship.
content:
The Mason County Royals and Augusta Panthers took to the floor of the Fieldhouse Thursday evening for the 39th district boys' basketball championship.
The Royals and Panthers saw one another twice in the regular season, with Mason County taking the first contest 80-52 early in the season, and Augusta the second 74-72 in late January. Both teams having picked up a win over one another in the regular season, they were each aiming for a strong performance in the championship game.
A win in this contest would mean nine straight district titles for Mason County, winning each since Augusta's last championship victory in 2016.
Both teams were working hard to hold off one another's offenses in the early minutes of the game, Mason County picking up a slim lead by the end of the first quarter, heading into the second up 8-7 over the Panthers. A slow start offensively for both Mason County and Augusta, the contest would slowly begin to heat up throughout the remainder of the first half.
'I think there was a lot of jitters there in the early going. It was an electric atmosphere, we haven't seen that a whole lot throughout the course of the year, but our kids finally settled down and saw some shots go in.' said Royals head coach, Brian Kirk, 'It was a physical game from start to finish. We missed a lot of easy shots where we could've extended the lead there into the second half. The easy shots around the rim, and the free throws that we missed, we've gotta capitalize on those if we want to advance in the region.'
Mason County's shooters came alive in the second quarter, outscoring the Panthers 18-6, for a 26-13 lead heading into halftime. Despite the 13 point deficit, Augusta was eager to return to the court in the third quarter, looking to close the gap and mark a late game comeback.
The Panthers fought hard throughout the third, able to slow down the Mason County offense and outscore the Royals 21-17. At the end of the quarter, with just over a second left on the clock, Mason County freshman Jace Merz was standing under Augusta's goal to inbound the ball. A huge pass from Merz to Cole Horch would secure Mason County's last goal of the quarter.
'That's just kids making plays. Most importantly, that was a heck of a pass from Jace Merz. Then you got a top notch wide receiver who's done that on the football field. He's done that, catching footballs, basketballs up over top somebody's head, then most importantly finishing the play. Heck of a pass, heck of a catch, heck of a play. Big momentum shift for us going into the fourth quarter.' said coach Kirk.
Heading into the final few minutes of play, Mason County led 43-34, and looked to maintain their lead throughout the fourth quarter and secure their ninth district championship. Augusta, still refusing to back down, continued to fight to close the gap, still hoping for a chance to pull ahead late in the contest.
Another strong quarter offensively from the Royals would see Mason County put up 22 more, outscoring Augusta by 10. A 19 point lead at the buzzer, Mason County picked up another win over Augusta, up 65-46 over the Panthers. Following the Royals' 83-56 win over Bracken County in the district semifinals, coach Kirk said they were looking to redeem their prior loss to the Panthers, and were able to pull out a strong, decisive victory when it mattered most.
'I mean, we used it as motivation for our kids. I think people panicked back in January. Streaks end, history repeats itself. I don't care who you are, where you're at, streaks eventually end, and I think that was the best thing for our kids. This team is extremely well coached, they play hard and they're capable beating anybody and I think we used that as motivation.' said coach Kirk.
With this win, the Royals now prepare for the upcoming 10th region boys' basketball tournament, held this year at Montgomery County, a week later than normal.
The boys' 10th region basketball tournament is set to begin Monday, March 10, at Montgomery County High School, with teams drawing for opponents this morning. Both Mason County and Augusta will spend the week off planning and preparing for what will undoubtedly be a tough run through the region, on the way to the 2025 boys' sweet 16 state tournament.
'We're definitely gonna enjoy this one, we'll probably take the weekend off. This year's a little different set up, time wise as we've got an entire week to prepare. We're definitely gonna enjoy this one and this weekend, find out who we play on Saturday morning and start our prep, come back in next week and start to put the things together.' said coach Kirk.

title: Lady Royals drop to GRC
description: The Mason County Lady Royals took on the George Rogers Clark Lady Cardinals in the first round of the 10th region girls' basketball tournament on Monday.
content:
The Mason County Lady Royals took on the George Rogers Clark Lady Cardinals in the first round of the 10th region girls' basketball tournament on Monday.
Mason County, entering the tournament district runners-up after falling to the Bracken County Lady Bears 63-48 in the 39th district championship, drew three time defending 10th region champions, the GRC Lady Cardinals for the first round of the 10th region tournament, and immediately began preparing. Prior to this contest, the Lady Cardinals were ranked first in the region according to RPI, with a 22-7 season record, going undefeated against 10th region teams, and 8-0 in the 40th district.
Despite the tough challenge that lay ahead, the Lady Royals entered the contest ready to go, and were looking to put up a strong performance against one of the 10th region's strongest.
'We kinda put on the board coming into these last couple days, mindset was gonna be so important in how we wanted to approach this. I knew they were down, not winning the district which was definitely a huge goal of ours, and that makes the draw a little tougher, and you end up drawing one of the best teams in the state of Kentucky.' said Lady Royals head coach, Jay Fite, 'It took us a day to knock the cobwebs off and then be ready to come back in and start battling, competing in practice. I had a feeling we were gonna come in and plug away. I told them before the game started, I don't wanna see anything negative, I just want to see everybody going all out for 32 minutes.'
Early on in the first quarter, both teams defenses worked hard to prevent the opposition from scoring, the first goal of the night going to George Rogers Clark over a minute into the contest. The game would remain 2-0 for a considerable amount of the first quarter, before the Lady Cardinals were able to expand upon their two point lead, up 14-3 over Mason County heading into the second quarter.
Throughout the remainder of the first half, GRC would continue to pull away from Mason County, despite the Lady Royals finally finding the basket. The Lady Cardinals would outscore Mason County 25-11 this quarter, for a 39-14 lead heading into halftime.
'We really struggled to score on our end. They're super defensively. They're a great team and our biggest goals were trying to take care of it and we really didn't turn it over in the full court, but we did once we got down to the half court. At times we weren't able to get into much, get into too many sets. And then, losing Lexi early, losing AP early, that kinda affects some things, and the ease that we can get into some things. Credit Clark County, Robbie Graham's a tremendous coach and they've got a tremendous program. They are the standard in our region, and one of the standards in the state of Kentucky.' said coach Fite.
Upon returning to the court after halftime, the Lady Cardinals looked to further their lead over Mason County, while the Lady Royals hoped to stay in the fight, and continue putting up a strong performance against GRC.
Another strong quarter offensively for the Lady Cards would see them outscore Mason County 21-16, for a 60-30 lead heading into the final quarter of the contest. 17 more scored by GRC this quarter would round out the Lady Cardinals' scoring this game, holding Mason County to just seven, for a 77-37 victory for the three time reigning 10th region champions.
Despite the loss, and the 2024-25 season coming to an end for the Mason County Lady Royals, coach Fite and his team walked off the court with their heads held high, excited for an even stronger season come 2025-26. With no seniors on the roster, all of Mason County's lineup are eager to return to the court, and continue improving their game under coach Fite.
'It's a great thing, that's what I told the kids. It's taken us some time for me to get to know them this year. It's been an every day process for us. Once I've gotten to know them, the more you like them, the more you care about them and the more you want to see them succeed. I think now that they know that I'm pushing for them, I'm pulling for them and I'm here for them, I'm not here for any other reason than to try to make them better players and people.' said coach Fite, 'Hopefully we can continue trying to display that on the floor, but it's really exciting to have these kids and an off-season that we didn't have last year. I think it's gonna be an exciting season next year.'
With this win, the George Rogers Clark Lady Cardinals now move on to face the Campbell County Lady Camels in the semifinal round of the girls' 10th region tournament Friday evening at 6:00 p.m., at Campbell County Middle School.
