**********
'Shut the door. Not that it lets in the cold but that it lets out the coziness.' – Mark Twain

title: Cats still a work in progress
author: Chuck Hamilton
description: Kentucky's 70-66 loss in front of a rowdy Clemson crowd on Tuesday night should serve as an eye-opener to head coach Mark Pope and his players.
content:
Kentucky's 70-66 loss in front of a rowdy Clemson crowd on Tuesday night should serve as an eye-opener to head coach Mark Pope and his players.
Opponents are going to repeat the formula employed by the Tigers as they try to knock off the Wildcats. The physical style used by Clemson helped them give the Cats their first loss of the season. Earlier, less talented opponents–Western Kentucky and Georgia State immediately come to mind–have also attempted to upset UK by being extra physical.
Kentucky relies on more of a finesse game, and likes to shoot the 3, but when they're not falling, the team needs to find other ways to score.
Rebounding, and especially giving up offensive boards, is another aspect of the game that the Cats need to improve upon. When game-planning for UK, opposing coaches are also going to notice the team's free-throw shooting has been less than impressive, meaning if they commit a few more fouls by playing a more physical brand of basketball, they will take that risk.
It's still early, and this group assembled by Pope and his staff in rapid fashion is still learning how to play together, which gives me confidence they will continue to improve and develop better chemistry during the season. The veteran roster should also serve itself well going forward. If Kentucky has hopes of contending in the SEC, and advancing in the postseason—and of course that is the goal—improvement in several areas will be imperative.
Another huge test awaits the Cats this evening in matchup that has been billed the Battle in Seattle, when Kentucky meet another physical team, but one that likes to run and shoot threes as well. The game versus Gonzaga also represents a return home for Pope, who hails from the Seattle suburb of Bellevue, and began his collegiate career at the University of Washington. That also means he is quite familiar with the Zags and their winning tradition. They enter this one with a 7-1 record,
with their lone defeat coming in the Battle 4 Atlantis tournament to West Virginia in a surprising 86-78 loss.
The Cats will be trying to avenge an 89-85 loss to Gonzaga in Rupp Arena last season. Of course, that was with a completely different roster and coaching staff in Lexington, but the Zags have several key returnees, including 6-9 senior Graham Ike, 6-10 sophomore Braden Huff, 6-2 senior Nolan Hickman and 6-foot senior Ryan Nembhard. They feature a balanced scoring attack, with the aforementioned players all averaging in double digits. An Arkansas transfer, 6-5 graduate student Khalif Battle, is another key player for the Zags, averaging 13.5 points per game.
It will be another stern test for Kentucky, who may be without the services of the player who runs the team from his point guard position, Lamont Butler. Butler tweaked his ankle at Clemson and the drop-off was obvious when he left the lineup, first with foul trouble, and later with the injury. The UK depth is in need of a boost, but the hope is they will be able to pick up their play and give Pope positive minutes in the near future.
It will be interesting as well to see if the Cats can have a better shooting night from behind the arc, where they've been struggling of late, including just 7-for-27 (25.9%) in Tuesday's loss. Another area of concern is at the stripe, where they converted just 11-of-18 for just 61.1%.
Summing it up, this should be a whale of a college basketball game, even though the start time of 10 p.m. is less than desirable. Even if the Cats are unable to notch a win in this one, it shouldn't alarm UK fans all that much. It's actually a good thing they're playing great competition, and as long as they learn and grow from the experience, it will be a positive in the long run. It will certainly not get any easier when they begin conference play against Florida next month.
**********
REDS IN MIX FOR ANOTHER STARTER – Rumors are running rampant, which is always the case during December in Major League Baseball.
The annual MLB Winter Meetings begin Monday, a time when general managers convene and do their best Monty Hall impersonation and say, 'Let's Make a Deal.' (For the younger folks out there, you will have to do a Google search to understand the reference.)
For the Cincinnati Reds, things could get extremely interesting real soon. The latest trade rumor has the Reds acquiring left-handed starter Garrett Crochet from the Chicago White Sox in exchange for four prospects, including infielders Sal Stewart and Sammy Stafura, along with pitchers Chase Petty and Lyon Richardson. Cincy may have a bidding war with division rival Chicago Cubs in its quest for another quality starting pitcher, and if the Reds are willing to part with a few prospects, they may just be able to pull it off. They may also need to include a player off the big league roster, but if they can swing a deal without giving up the farm, it says here they should do whatever it takes to get it done.
Crochet, the 1th overall selection of the 2020 MLB Draft out of the University of Tennessee, made 32 starts for the woeful ChiSox last year, and finished 6-12 with a 3.58 ERA in 146 innings, to go with 209 strikeouts. That win-loss record could be reversed with a team that doesn't break records for futility, like the White Sox did last year, finishing with a 41-121 record.
The 6-foot-6 southpaw is 25 years old and was named the American League Comeback Player of the Year following a return from Tommy John surgery. Crochet is also under team control for a couple of years, making him even more attractive. For those who cry out that the Reds have enough starting pitchers, my retort is that you can never have enough quality pitching, and acquiring Crochet could mean one of the Reds starters may be included in another move to pick up an outfield bat, and perhaps some help for the bullpen.
That brings us to another rumor, one that says the Reds may giving up on closer Alexis Diaz, and discussions may already be taking place to send him elsewhere. The return would have to be a bat with some power potential, something the Cincinnati lineup desperately needs.
Another recent rumor suggests that the Reds may have some interest in bringing Jesse Winker back to the Queen City. Not too keen about this possibility, but if the team is unable to sign a power hitter to be their designated hitter, Winker may be an option. I would much prefer a player who possesses more power, perhaps Joc Pederson. It is doubtful the club will sign any of the higher-priced free agents, such as Teoscar Hernandez or Anthony Santander, but the 2024 season showed us the Reds desperately need more pop in the lineup.
You can rest assured that more and more rumors will be popping up in the coming days and weeks, and here's hoping the Cincinnati front office can get the pieces needed to make a run in 2025. Reds president of baseball operations Nick Krall recently said the club is looking to add hitters, and whether it's in a trade or free agency, there are plenty of options.
**********
'Basketball isn't just a sport. It is an art, one that must be mastered to succeed.' – Stephen Curry
**********
'Rumor will die itself if you only give it three days. Start any rumor, and if the public can go with its curiosity unsatisfied for three days something else will spring up which will make the public forget all about the first one.' – Mark Twain

title: Royals, Lady Royals off to a strong start
description: The Mason County Royals and Lady Royals got the basketball season started at the Fieldhouse on Monday.
content:
The Mason County Royals and Lady Royals got the basketball season started at the Fieldhouse on Monday.
In their first of two district seed games against the St. Pat Saints and Lady Saints, both Mason County teams looked to come out strong, hungry to end their season openers with a win.
In the first game of the night, the Lady Royals jumped out ahead of the Lady Saints quickly, leading 28-9 over St. Pat by the end of the first quarter. Mason County would then continue to build upon this lead, up 76-16 by the end of the third to roll to an 89-24 final score at the end of the 32 minutes of regulation.
Amirah Reed led the Lady Royals in scoring this game, picking up 26 points across three two-point field goals, six three's and two free throws. Coming in just behind her was Lexi Young, with 14 total points, making six two-point field goals, and two baskets from the free throw line. Reed also led the team in rebounds, with three.
After pulling out a decisive victory in his debut as head coach of the Lady Royals, Jay Fite continues to look forward to leading his team throughout the 2024-25 season, as they aim for another 2A state tournament appearance, a district championship and a deep run into the 10th region tournament.
Following this contest, the Royals and Saints tipped off, with the Mason County boys team hoping for a similar outcome.
At the end of the first eight minutes of play, the Royals led 22-3 over St. Pat, a lead they would quickly deepen as the contest continued. Mason County was up 47-8 at halftime, and ended the contest leading 79-18. A strong start for the Royals, now 1-0 in the 39th district after their first seed game of the year.
Cole Horch and Braxton Malone were tied for first for the Royals in scoring this game, both putting up 14 total points. Horch had seven two-point field goals, with Malone scoring one, and four from behind the three-point line. Standout sophomore Braeden Myrick then scored 12 for Mason County, across three two-point field goals, and two three's.
The Saints were led in scoring by Abisai Ignacio, putting up 10 of St. Pat's 18 total points across eight field goals and two free throws.
After a strong win for the Royals in their home opener of the 2024-25 season, the team, and head coach Brian Kirk now gear up to check off many of their goals for this year, with a strong performance in the 2A sectional, a 2A state appearance, their ninth straight 39th district championship and a deep run into the 10th region tournament.
Following these contests, the Royals then took on the Rowan County Vikings on Tuesday, with the Lady Royals gearing up to face Eastern Brown this evening. Both teams will then head to Augusta on Saturday to take on the Panthers and Lady Panthers in another district seed doubleheader, starting at 6:00 p.m., with the Royals and Panthers tipping off first.

title: Stupid is as stupid does
author: Chuck Hamilton
description: You may think I'm stupid for even attempting to begin today's piece with the above headline taken from the film Forrest Gump. That's quite alright; Lord knows I have made more than a few stupid…
content:
You may think I'm stupid for even attempting to begin today's piece with the above headline taken from the film Forrest Gump. That's quite alright; Lord knows I have made more than a few stupid decisions in my life. This idea may be considered another one, but try to hear me out.
Stupid was the first word that popped into my brain when the Michigan football team tried to plant a school flag at midfield at Ohio Stadium following its improbable upset win over the Buckeyes. The same scenario has occurred at other venues as well, and in my humble opinion, it's far from an intelligent decision. The retaliation from angered Ohio State players is understandable, but the entire situation was completely unnecessary, classless, and yes, stupid.
At the risk of coming off as an old fogey, another stupid move made far too often in college athletics is storming the field or court of play following an unexpected win. Eventually, serious injuries are going to occur to innocent people who are in the wrong place at the wrong time.
While we're on the subject of stupid, how about MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred's most recent ridiculous idea?
If you haven't heard, the gimmicky Manfred has proposed is something called the 'Golden At Bat' rule. The rule would allow teams to pick one spot per game in which their best hitter could pop into the batter's box regardless of what the lineup says. Coming up with such a silly notion approaches the ultimate in stupidity. The idea is even more stupid than his 'ghost runner' on second base beginning in extra-inning games rule that he brought to MLB several years ago.
One more stupid sports item on my mind lately is the Associated Press Top 25 Men's College Basketball Poll. The stupidity level doesn't rise to the level of the aforementioned examples, but you have to wonder what some of these voters are thinking when they turn in their weekly ballots.
I realize the poll is, for the most part, meaningless, and serves its purpose for folks to argue about where the teams are placed. This week's stupid example is having 7-2 Duke ranked fourth, and Kentucky (8-1) one spot below the Blue Devils, despite the Cats knocking off Duke earlier in the season.
**********
COMEBACK CATS, PART II – The 1997-1998 Kentucky Wildcats earned the nickname 'Comeback Cats' while on their way to winning what many considered an unlikely run to a national championship. This year's group is
doing a pretty fair job of emulating that team in the still early season.
The latest comeback was improbable and completely unexpected, when coach Mark Pope and his resilient bunch of Wildcats stormed back from a 16-point halftime deficit to catch and pass Gonzaga in Seattle on Saturday night.
Clutch performances in the second half from Jaxson Robinson and Andrew Carr led the resurgent Cats to the overtime triumph. The Zags were on the verge of achieving a blowout win after leading 50-34 at the break, and confounding the UK defense in the process.
Not so fast, my friend.
After Pope made a few halftime adjustments, including going to a 1-3-1 zone, Kentucky steadily seized momentum and eventually clawed their way back, and held off the Bulldogs in the extra session.
The game, which resembled something we may see in March, featured a little bit of everything. There were outstanding plays from both teams, and huge shots made at key moments, especially by Robinson, who was used at the point when back-up Kerr Kriisa went down with an ankle injury after tossing in eight points and dishing out four assists. Kriisa, who was in the starting lineup due to an injury to starting point guard Lamont Butler, is expected to be out for several weeks.
Along with the contributions from Carr (19 points, seven rebounds) and Robinson (18 points, five assists), several other Cats stepped up to erase the 18-point second half deficit. Otega Oweh and Amari Williams dropped in 13 and 12 points respectively, and Brandon Garrison played an outstanding 17 minutes off the bench (with the exception of three turnovers.) The 6-foot-10 Oklahoma State transfer scored 10 key points and grabbed a team-high nine boards.
After tonight's expected cakewalk against 2-8 Colgate – in Rupp Arena, the Battle of the Bluegrass looms early Saturday evening. Kentucky will be hosting the Louisville Cardinals in the annual grudge match. The Cats are hoping to have Butler back and ready to play against the Cards in what should be an intensely played and entertaining affair. We'll have more to say about that one in the Saturday column.
**********
BENGALS (FINALLY) CATCH A BREAK – It has been well documented that this year's Cincinnati Bengals haven't been blessed by the football gods.
Perhaps that is taking a turn for the better following the team's fortuitous 27-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football. In what looked to be another one-score defeat after the Cowboys blocked a Ryan Rehkow punt late in the game, good fortune at last
smiled upon the Men in Stripes. Former Bengal Nick Vigil appeared to be the hero for Dallas after he blocked the punt, but the Cowboys' Amani Oruwariye did the visitors a huge favor by trying to field the carom, but he fumbled it away, resulting in a Cincinnati recovery to set up quarterback Joe Burrow and the offense.
Joe B and Ja'Marr Chase did the rest, when the LSU connection did its thing. Chase broke away for a 40-yard touchdown reception with 1:01 left, and the Bengals were able to celebrate with a rare win in Big D. As usual, the pair put up ridiculous numbers, with Burrow going 33-of-44 through the air for 369 yards and three scores, while the smiling Chase caught 14 passes for 177 yards and two TDs.
The Who Deys improved to 5-8 on the season and still need at least a couple of miracles to earn a postseason bid, but it was a fun night in Jerry World for a team that hasn't had much fun (or gotten many breaks) this year.
**********
FELDHAUS OFF TO GOOD START – Former Mason County forward Jake Feldhaus is apparently finding his new home in Richmond to his liking. Madison Central is off to a 3-0 start in the early going, and Feldhaus, who is now playing for his uncle, longtime Indians head coach Allen Feldhaus Jr., is adapting quite well to his new surroundings.
The 6-foot-5 junior is averaging 17.7 points and a team-leading 14 rebounds per game, and collected 19 boards in the team's most recent win, a 67-58 victory over Corbin on Saturday. The Indians opened with a 65-57 win at Pulaski County before an 88-49 thrashing of Lafayette. Junior Luke Asher leads Madison Central in scoring at 22.7 per outing.
The 11th Region team faced their biggest test of the young season in Winchester on Tuesday evening, after this was written. They faced another 3-0 squad and the consensus team to beat in the 10th Region, George Rogers Clark. The Cardinals opened with home victories over Nicholas County (89-67) and Campbell County (59-42) before a 77-53 win on the road at Pendleton County on Saturday. GRC is led by junior Malachi Ashford and sophomore Montez Gay, who are scoring 16.3 and 15 points per game, respectively.
**********
'I'll call somebody 'dumb' or 'stupid' if they make a dumb or stupid play. I don't know any other word for it, and if they don't like the word, that's too bad.' – Bill Parcells
********** 'I may be dumb, but I'm not stupid.' – Terry Bradshaw
********** 'He was endowed with a stupidity which by the least
little stretch would go around the globe four times and tie.' – Mark Twain

title: Celebrate Christmas Every Day
author: Albert Earley
description: Have you ever heard of Andy Park, a.k.a. Mr. Christmas? On July 14, 1993, this Englishman got the incredible idea to celebrate Christmas daily. To do this, he decided to have mincemeat pie and sherry for breakfast, roast turkey, potatoes, and brussel sprouts for lunch, and at 3:00 p.m., watch the Queen's Christmas speech while drinking a glass of champagne. I could not find out if he is continuing this tradition today, but as of 2006, Park was quoted as saying that he had consumed 4,380 turkeys, 87,600 mince pies, 2,190 pints of gravy, 26,280 roasted potatoes, 4,380 bottles of both champagne and sherry.
content:
Have you ever heard of Andy Park, a.k.a. Mr. Christmas? On July 14, 1993, this Englishman got the incredible idea to celebrate Christmas daily. To do this, he decided to have mincemeat pie and sherry for breakfast, roast turkey, potatoes, and brussel sprouts for lunch, and at 3:00 p.m., watch the Queen's Christmas speech while drinking a glass of champagne. I could not find out if he is continuing this tradition today, but as of 2006, Park was quoted as saying that he had consumed 4,380 turkeys, 87,600 mince pies, 2,190 pints of gravy, 26,280 roasted potatoes, 4,380 bottles of both champagne and sherry.
I have challenged my congregation to celebrate Christmas daily, but I never imagined one would do it this way. Today I want to challenge you with being a peacemaker. At Christmas time, we often hear this text from Isaiah 9:6, 'For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.' Jesus said, 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God' (Matthew 5:9). Do you know how to be a peacemaker?
If you answered a resounding, 'I am not sure,' join the club. During covid, God worked hard on my prayer life, specifically equipping me for spiritual battles by putting on the armor of God (Ephesians 6:10-18). I would pray through the six pieces of armor, asking God to equip me, but I had no idea what 'feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace.' I kept praying for understanding, and God led me to craft the prayer how He wanted it.
First, He showed me the world we live in is a world of chaos, and all around me are people whose lives are chaotic because of this. As I prayed for them, God reminded me how often Jesus found He was surrounded by chaos, too. For example, when the Pharisees brought the woman caught in adultery to test Jesus. He was the perfect example of peace as He exposed the Pharisees' hypocrisy (John 8:1-11).
Second, I realized that I was rarely an example of peace in my world of chaos. Through prayer, God showed me how to stop feeding off the emotional energy of people struggling with chaos and focus on what God was doing in those situations. He reminded me He is always present in those situations, but I needed to pray, in the midst of the chaos, for Him to show me where He was. As I kept praying for my feet to be fitted with the gospel of peace, God changed me into an example of peace in chaotic situations.
Finally, He called me to be His hands, feet, and voice in chaotic situations. This included carrying myself confidently with the assurance of doing His work of peace and doing things that would communicate His presence. Even more, He wanted me to look for opportunities to pray over struggling people. God fills me with His Spirit in these prayers and miraculously blesses those being prayed for.
God tested me one day as a pickup truck ran a red light and smashed the back of an SUV. The SUV was spinning fast, right for my car. I knew I was going to be walloped by this car that was twice the size of my car, but I calmly prayed, 'Lord, please protect me.' About ten feet from my car, the SUV suddenly spun right, spinning to a halt on the gravel shoulder and hitting nothing. I could see God was present, protecting people in miraculous ways.
I jumped out of my car and checked on the truck driver, who was fine. When I got to the SUV, the woman was in a full panic attack. She was able to let me know she wasn't hurt, but spinning continuously for about fifty feet had left her understandably upset. I asked her if I could pray for her. The prayer was much better than any prayer I could pray. I knew God was giving me the words. As I prayed, I watched God's Spirit settle on her and give her peace. The panic attack disappeared. When I said, 'Amen,' she said, 'Thank you,' in a miraculously calm voice.
Do you know how to be a peacemaker? Have you ever submitted yourself to God to help bring peace to the chaos around you? Have you ever prayed for someone in their moment of chaos? I hope you will meet Jesus, the Prince of Peace, in a new way this Christmas! (To learn more about Al Earley or read previous articles see, www.lagrangepres.org).

title: Day 20: Erin Williams
description: The Ledger Independent is publishing a 50/50 series featuring 50 things over 50 weeks. During this series, our readers can expect to see different 'Local Talents/Artisans' each week.
content:
The Ledger Independent is publishing a 50/50 series featuring 50 things over 50 weeks. During this series, our readers can expect to see different 'Local Talents/Artisans' each week.
Some of the 'Local Talents/Artisans' that may be featured will include artists, authors, songwriters and more. The general definition of 'artisan' refers to a worker in a skilled trade, according to the Oxford Dictionary.
Please enjoy Day 20 of the series.
Erin Williams has been working with clay for more than 10 years after developing a skill and love for it.
Williams, a native of Maysville, studied at The University of Indianapolis as an art therapy major.
After graduating college and having completed an apprenticeship in Whitefish, Mont. as well as an artist residency in Columbia, Mo., Williams returned to Maysville in 2022 with her husband and three cats.
'I hadn't touched clay in any academic setting. I was required to take a ceramic course for my major. I actually didn't fall head over heels in love with the clay at the first touch,' Williams said.
She noted that the clay flew off onto the floor the first time she threw on a potter's wheel.
'It was a slow romance that required nurturing and hard work on my part. With every ceramic class I took, my skill and love for it deepened, though. By the time I graduated I knew that I needed to continue to make art with clay,' Williams expressed.
According to Williams, the majority of her artwork is made from a potter's wheel but she also uses additional elements like hand building including her recent work of 'Beans' and 'Florever Arrangements'.
'My favorite thing to make on the potter's wheel is a mug, though, because it's a part of so many people's routine whether it has coffee, tea, or anything else in it. Drinking vessels can elevate something as simple as having coffee with a friend,' Williams said.
She expressed that since her art is handmade 'it connects you to something larger than yourself' and it makes her feel 'part of something greater.'
'Through my art, I am able to work through emotions, thoughts and ideas. In that way my art is therapy for me,' Williams noted.
She expressed that the clay beans that she makes which are sold at EAT Gallery in downtown Maysville 'were conceived after the loss of a friend.'
'Needing to create something joyful after a period of grief was essential in my healing. Whether it's the imagery I paint onto my pottery or looking at the colorful beans, my hope is that others see my art and find a connection that gives them what they need like creating it gives me what I need,' Williams stated.
She explained that she has a home studio and offers classes for people to take.
You can learn more about Williams and her pottery on her website, erinwilliamspottery.com.

title: Coach Wynn headed to Simon Kenton
description: Mason County Royals head football coach Joe Wynn has resigned from the program.
content:
Mason County Royals head football coach Joe Wynn has resigned from the program.
Since taking over the program in 2021, Wynn led the Royals through four successful seasons, leaving Mason County with a 36-14 record. His first year with the team the Royals went 9-4, reaching the region semifinals, after not making the playoffs in 2020. Each year since, Mason County has seen playoff competition, and has worked hard to reach the state championship.
In 2022, Wynn and the Royals went undefeated throughout the regular season, flying past each of their opponents and bringing home a district, and region championship. That season they advanced to the state semifinals, falling 38-28 to a tough Bardstown Tigers team.
The next year, the Royals were moved up to the 4A division, with a new district of opponents to face.
Mason County ended 2023 6-5, picking up wins against several tough opponents, and defeated all of their district opponents with the exception of their new district rivals, the Covington Catholic Colonels. The Royals went on to host the Boyd County Lions, where they fell 14-7 in the first round of the Class 4A playoffs.
This past season, Mason County once again came out swinging, going 8-4 on the season. With just three regular season losses, a 3-0 battle against Boyd County, a 49-0 drop to Cov-Cath, and a 49-20 loss to Lawrence County, the Royals geared up for their second trip to the 4A playoffs. In the first round, Mason County put up a strong performance against the Greenup County Musketeers, pulling ahead for a 59-21 victory, before taking to Ashland to battle the Tomcats. There, the Royals fell 42-14, putting an end to another strong Mason County football season.
Following that contest, Wynn said, 'The best title I think in life you can have is a dad and a husband and a brother, but outside of family the greatest title I can have is to be their football coach. I told them that pregame. We play for each other, we play hard and we competed our tails off. They're destined for great things in life through the hard work and dedication they put in these four years.'
Since taking over the program, the longstanding rivalry between the Royals and Fleming County Panthers has remained a top priority for Mason County. The Royals dropped 12-7 to the Panthers in the 2021 regular season, but haven't lost a game to Fleming County since, picking up an 8-0 victory in the playoffs that year, ending a Fleming County nine game win streak over the Royals.
Throughout their next few contests, Mason County pulled out a 40-28 victory, a 49-21 win over the Panthers in 2023 and a 54-20 win this past year.
After defeating Fleming County on their home field this season, Wynn said, 'Beat the Panthers, that's one of our goals and the first goal in the season is to obviously win every game, but from a benchmark we wanna beat the Panthers, beat Cov-Cath, win region and go compete for a state title. One step down.'
Next season, Wynn will be leading the charge for the 6A Simon Kenton Pioneers.
The Pioneers ended 2024 4-7, picking up wins over Dixie Heights, Mercer County, Ballard and Campbell County. Their season came to an end in the first round of the 6A playoffs, where they fell 48-13 to the St. Xavier Tigers.
Wynn's goal at Simon Kenton will be to rebuild the program and start bringing in wins early in 2025, as they look to advance deep into the 6A playoffs.
Four successful seasons with the Royals, a 36-14 career record at Mason County, one of the most successful seasons in program history and a 4-1 record against one of the team's biggest rivals. Wynn helped the Royals succeed these past four seasons, and will be missed by his team, but he is eager to take on the Pioneers and start preparing them for a strong 2025 season.

title: KYGMC's 2024 outreach brings national and global visitors to Maysville
description: The Kentucky Gateway Museum Center saw many visitors in 2024 spanning many states and global nations.
content:
The Kentucky Gateway Museum Center saw many visitors in 2024 spanning many states and global nations.
KYGMC Executive Director Robert Boone expressed that the museum sees most of its visitors in the spring, summer and fall.
'Most of our visitors in 2024 and all past years come from Kentucky, especially the northern Kentucky and Cincinnati area. Although we did see growth in reaching the central Kentucky, Lexington area, in 2024. Globally, most of our visitors are concentrated in the United Kingdom and western Europe regions,' Boone said.
He explained that most of the museum visitors especially those from Europe, visit to see the KSB Miniatures Collection.
'Visitors usually find us via the web, social media, conferences and tour groups,' Boone stated.
In 2024, KYGMC had a visitor count of around 7,583 according to Boone. He noted that the number included those who visited the museum.
'This number does not include outreach outside of the walls of the KYGMC. If we add the outreach numbers to the 7,583, then our reach grows to about 20,000 people,' Boone said.
He further expressed that the museum's outreach included on-site educational programming for around 20 schools that was delivered regularly and the annual Big Read.
'In 2024, the KYGMC hosted two conferences in the spring. We were the host site for the spring Kentucky Museum and Heritage Alliance Conference, which brought visitors from across Kentucky. Also in the spring, the KYGMC was the host for the KSB Miniatures Workshops, which brought visitors from around the world,' Boone stated.
KYGMC Trustee Emeritus Louis Browning expressed that in 2024 visitors came from 48 states and the District of Columbia along with 18 countries and dozens of cities in Kentucky.
He further noted that after four days into the new year, KYGMC welcomed visitors from six states and four countries.
'As for 2025, we will host new exhibits in our two changing galleries, including a really great 'Thomas The Train' interactive exhibit geared toward children that we have borrowed from the Minneapolis Children's Museum,' Boone stated.
He further expressed;
'We will also increase our evening lecture series, covering a variety of topics. Finally, we will be launching an oral history collection lab and initiative that will enable us to further preserve our region's history,' said Boone.
Browning stated that KYGMC is excited to meet everyone who will visit the museum in 2025 and that they are grateful to those who visited in 2024.

title: A review of the past week, with a preview looming
author: Chuck Hamilton
description: While trying to decide what to touch on for the midweek missive – and waiting for my fingers to thaw – I concluded that I would make a feeble attempt at commenting on a few things that occurred over the past weekend. A look back, if you will, with the plan for the Saturday column being a peek at an action-packed sports weekend, concluding with the College Football Playoff Championship Game on Monday night.
content:
While trying to decide what to touch on for the midweek missive – and waiting for my fingers to thaw – I concluded that I would make a feeble attempt at commenting on a few things that occurred over the past weekend. A look back, if you will, with the plan for the Saturday column being a peek at an action-packed sports weekend, concluding with the College Football Playoff Championship Game on Monday night.
*****
CATS PICK UP SOLID ROAD WIN – Coach Mark Pope and his veteran group of transfers continue to surprise many college basketball observers. Before the season began, not a lot was said among the national experts about the all-new roster of Kentucky Wildcats, primarily because the team began the year shrouded in mystery. As the season has progressed, the team is finding its identity, and shown it can be a force to be reckoned with, including against some of the best teams in the country.
The 95-90 road win at Mississippi State was nothing to sneeze at, after all the 14-2 Bulldogs are a formidable foe, and the raucous home crowd was smelling blood from the opening tip.
Jaxson Robinson came to the rescue for the Cats, putting together his most glittering performance of the season. The BYU transfer came into the game in a serious shooting slump, but broke out with a game-high 27 points, including 7-of-10 from deep.
It doesn't get any easier for Pope and the 8th-ranked Cats, who played the No. 11 Texas A&M Aggies on Tuesday evening, after this blurb was written. Both teams entered the fray with
identical 13-3 records, and 2-1 in SEC play. UK enters as a slight favorite as it hopes to snap a two-game losing streak to the Aggies, including a 97-87 setback in the SEC Tournament last year.
It gets even more challenging for Kentucky on Saturday afternoon, when 4th-ranked Alabama visits Lexington in highly anticipated game we will preview more in depth on Saturday. The high-flying Crimson Tide is 14-2 after a 94-88 win at Texas A&M last Saturday. They hosted No. 21 Ole Miss on Tuesday.
*****
NFL DOWN TO FINAL EIGHT– Most of the NFL Wild Card Weekend was a colossal snooze fest.
In the AFC, the Buffalo Bills cruised to a 31-7 win over outmatched Denver, the upstart Houston Texans embarrassed the Los Angeles Chargers 32-12, and Baltimore ran all over Pittsburgh in a 28-14 yawner.
The NFC slate began with another boring contest on Sunday afternoon when the Philadelphia Eagles disposed of Green Bay, 22-10, before Sunday Night Football delivered with a game worth watching. That's when the visiting Washington Commanders rallied for a 23-20 win over the Tampa Bay Bucs. Rookie quarterback Jayden Daniels continues to impress for the team that used to be known as the Redskins. The former LSU standout threw for 268 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions while adding a team-high 36 rushing yards. The calm and cool Daniels led the game-winning drive after the Buccaneers tied the game with a field goal. The Commanders did have a bit of luck on their side when the game-winning field
goal by Zane Gonzalez doinked off the right upright and went through as time expired.
Washington has enjoyed a remarkable turnaround under new ownership, featuring first-year head coach Dan Quinn, a group of unheralded players, and of course, their brilliant rookie QB. The reward is a trip to Detroit to face the NFC's top seed, but who knows? Perhaps the ultimate underdog can do it again.
The final Wild Card game between the Los Angeles Rams and Minnesota Vikings was played Monday night in Glendale, Arizona, after the game scheduled to be a Rams home game in LA was moved due to the tragic wildfires in Southern California. This one quickly became yet another less than thrilling matchup, as the Rams jumped out to a 24-3 halftime lead in a 27-9 sleeper.
Despite most of the Wild Card Weekend matchups turning out to be mostly unwatchable, the upcoming Divisional Round looks intriguing, and hopefully, much more competitive as well. We'll have more to say about those games in a few days, highlighted by the Baltimore at Buffalo slobberknocker on Sunday evening.
*****
BUCKEYES ROLL INTO TITLE TILT – The Ohio State Buckeyes have responded in impressive fashion after laying a huge egg in their 13-10 home defeat to their hated rival to the North on November 30. All the Bucks have done is demolish Tennessee 42-17, thrash Oregon 41-21, and topple Texas in the Cotton Bowl 28-14, en route to an appearance on the biggest stage of them all in college football. The latest string of victories has opened the eyes of the oddsmakers, who have installed Ohio
State as 8.5-points favorites over Notre Dame to win the national championship next Monday night in Atlanta.
OSU will tangle with a team that has enjoyed their own resurgence following an embarrassing defeat. The Fighting Irish, who fell 16-14 at home to Northern Illinois way back on September 7, have won 13 in a row and won a hard-fought 27-24 battle with Penn State last week.
We will have more about this clash of historical college football powerhouses in the next column. An interesting tidbit: the teams have met just eight times, and Ohio State has defeated Notre Dame six consecutive times, with the most recent one coming September 23, 2023, a Buckeyes' 17-14 victory in South Bend. The only two Irish wins in the series were a long, long time ago; ND won 7-2 in 1936, and 18-13 the previous season.
*****
BUBBA SWITCHES SPORTS – Devoted Cincinnati Reds fans will remember the name Bubba Thompson. The outfielder earned a spot on the big-league roster last year after enjoying a solid spring training with the club.
For the first week of the regular season he was used exclusively as a pinch runner, but started against the New York Mets on April 7, going 1-3 with a broken-bat base hit. The following day, Thompson started against the Brewers, and went 1-4 with a double, which would ultimately be the last hit of his career. Over the next month, he went 0-10 in nine games before he was optioned to Double-A Chattanooga. Bubba hit .232 for the Lookouts before a brief stint at Triple-A Louisville, where he hit .160 in nine games.
Following his lackluster 2024 season, Thompson became a free agent, but he apparently is done with baseball.
A recent report from AL.com says the 26-year-old former Reds outfielder has enrolled at the University of South Alabama and joined their football team as a walk-on. Thompson, a first-round draft pick of the Texas Rangers, was also a highly recruited quarterback with offers from multiple SEC schools before deciding to play baseball.
*****
'I might go my whole life stealing money. I got paid to play basketball, which is a scam. I get paid to watch basketball, which is a scam.' – Charles Barkley
*****
'There is no such thing as shoulda, coulda, woulda. If you shoulda and coulda, you woulda.' – Pat Riley
*****
'To be good is noble, but to teach others how to be good is nobler – and less trouble.' — Mark Twain

title: It takes more than $$$ to win a title
author: Chuck Hamilton
description: If you will indulge for me for just a moment, here is my brief summation of the current weather situation: January.
content:
If you will indulge for me for just a moment, here is my brief summation of the current weather situation: January.
Ugh.
Now that that's out of the way, let's delve into a few happenings surrounding the wide, wonderful world of sports.
*****
BUCKEYES BEST IN ALL PHASES – In reference to the above headline, much has been made of the fact that the Ohio State Buckeyes have the highest paid roster in all of college football.
My response to that is, so what?
There are more than a few college football powerhouses that have been doling out large sums of money to players for years, but just because you spend millions on players and coaches, winning championships is far from guaranteed. Granted, it doesn't lessen your chances of success, but you still have to execute between the lines, and ward off other excellent teams to emerge with the crown.
You may not like it, but that's the way it is in college sports these days. Like I referenced earlier, this isn't really anything new, but with the NIL coming into play recently, paying for talent is out in the open for all to gripe about.
Ohio State deserves a tremendous amount of credit for rebounding from an embarrassing home loss to its bitter rival, and rallying down the stretch in dominating fashion. The Buckeyes also took advantage of the new 12-team playoff,
because if it hadn't gone into effect this season, they would not be hoisting the national championship hardware.
In a four-team scenario, Ohio State would've been on the outside looking in, and their rabid fanbase would've been calling for the head of coach Ryan Day on a platter for losing to Michigan again. That doesn't mean all is forgiven amongst the OSU fans, but winning their seventh national title should be more than enough to forget about one loss, even if it was to the hated Wolverines.
The Buckeyes jumped out to a 31-7 lead midway through the third quarter and appeared to be well on their way to a blowout victory, but Notre Dame – which also enjoyed a fantastic season – played with a ton of heart and made it a game by scoring a pair of touchdown passes from Riley Leonard to Jaden Greathouse to go with a couple of 2-point conversions to slice the OSU advantage to 31-23 with 4:14 left.
Ohio State had an answer and put the game away when the baby-faced assassin, quarterback Will Howard, lobbed a deep ball on a 3rd down play to freshman Jeremiah Smith for a 52-yard gain to the Irish's 10-yard line, setting up a short field goal to ice the game.
Howard was efficient, completing 17-of-21 pass attempts for 231 yard to go with his 57 yards rushing, while the spectacular Smith reeled in five receptions for 88 yards and a TD. Quinshon Judkins had a tremendous game as well, running for 100 yards on 11 carries and two scores on the ground, while adding a touchdown reception as well.
The Irish, who showed their resolve by climbing back into the game, received star performances from Leonard – 22-31, 265
yards passing and two scores to go with a rushing touchdown – and Greathouse, who finished with five catches for 128 yards, including those two touchdowns.
It doesn't make the defeat any easier to swallow – and their players were understandably upset after the game — but Notre Dame has nothing to be ashamed of after reaching the title game, which no one thought possible after their early season loss to Northern Illinois.
Irish coach Marcus Freeman is to be commended for the excellent 14-2 season enjoyed by Notre Dame, and the same can be said for OSU's Day, who led the Buckeyes to a 14-2 mark as well. Look for both teams to be among the 12 that reach the playoffs next season.
*****
CATS HOPE TO BOUNCE BACK (AGAIN) – After being outgunned by Alabama on Saturday afternoon, it's time for coach Mark Pope and his charges to regroup and plow forward in the never-ending challenge that is Southeastern Conference basketball.
The Crimson Tide did just that against the Wildcats, winning a road game after suffering a home defeat in its previous game, a 74-64 loss to Ole Miss. Bama broke out of its one-game slump in a big way at Rupp Arena, exploiting what appears to be the area in most need of improvement for the Cats.
That is obviously the team's inability to come up with stops when they're needed the most. Kentucky appears capable of fixing its defensive flaws, but it needs to be a team effort. They need to adjust to the seemingly inconsistent and incompetent SEC officiating and learn how to play effective defense without committing an inordinate number of fouls. Keeping opponents
off the offensive glass also continues to be a work in progress for the Cats
For all of the negative backlash associated with a league loss at home – and it's certainly no disgrace to lose to a team as talented as Alabama — the 14-4 Cats have the opportunity to pick up a road win on Saturday afternoon when they head south to Nashville. For those of you who haven't been paying attention however, getting a win at Vanderbilt is no easy assignment.
After all, Vandy fans call it 'Memorial Magic' for a reason with the latest example of the sorcery occurring Saturday. The determined Commodores held on for a 76-75 win over their bitter, orange-clad rivals and dropped highly-ranked Tennessee to 16-2 in the process. The Cats get a shot at the Vols next Tuesday evening in Knoxville, before their highly anticipated showdown versus Arkansas on Saturday, Feb. 1 at 9 p.m. The 'Dores had their own gargantuan challenge on Tuesday evening (after this was written) when they ventured to Tuscaloosa to face Alabama.
This is the deepest and strongest the SEC has ever been, and if you have an off night, you're going to suffer defeat.
Just ask former UK coach John Calipari.
His Arkansas Razorbacks are still searching for an identity. They have endured more than a few off nights on their way to their current 0-5 league record, tying them for the cellar with South Carolina. The Hogs host Georgia tonight, and Oklahoma on Saturday night before their trip to Lexington.
As of this writing on Tuesday morning, Auburn is all alone at the top of the standings at 5-0, and the Tigers are also the top-
ranked team in the country with a 17-1 mark. Alabama, Missouri and Ole Miss are tied at 4-1, followed by no less than six teams — Florida, Kentucky, Mississippi State, Texas A&M, Tennessee and Vanderbilt – with 3-2 SEC records.
*****
REDS SIGN RELIEVER, STILL NEED MORE DEPTH IN PEN – In an effort to bolster their bullpen, the Cincinnati Reds inked a familiar face to a minor league deal on Monday. Lefthander Alex Young, who had a productive 2023 season in the Queen City, will be among the plethora of arms who will be given an opportunity to make the big club in the spring. In '23, the 31-year-old Young made a career-high 63 appearances, fashioning a 3.86 ERA in 53 2/3 innings.
Pitchers who are expected to earn bullpen nods include closer Alexis Diaz, Emilio Pagan, Tony Santillan, Sam Moll and Brent Suter. That leaves at least three spots available, with several veterans expected to compete for the openings. Righthanders Graham Ashcraft, Carson Spiers, and Bryan Shaw, a favorite of new manager Terry Francona, will vie for long relief duties.
A pair of promising rookies, Zach Maxwell and Luis Mey, will likely begin the season in Louisville, but could be factors during the season at some point. That's how it stands at the moment, but look for president of baseball operations Nick Krall to sign another reliever or two in the near future.
As we've expressed ad nauseum, you can never have enough pitching, and even though the Reds' starting rotation is potentially a team strength, the inevitability of injuries is always a factor, and a strong bullpen is integral to being a contender.
*****
'Nothing means nothing. But it isn't really nothing, because nothing is something that isn't.' – Darryl Dawkins
*****
'Losing is the worst.' – Mark Pope
*****
'I love everybody. Some I love to be around, some I love to avoid, and others I'd love to punch in the face.' – Charles Barkley
*****
'Noise proves nothing. Often a hen who has merely laid an egg cackles as if she had laid an asteroid.' – Mark Twain

description: The Ledger Independent is publishing a 50/50 series featuring 50 things over 50 weeks. During this series, our readers can expect to see different 'Local Talents/Artisans' each week.
content:
The Ledger Independent is publishing a 50/50 series featuring 50 things over 50 weeks. During this series, our readers can expect to see different 'Local Talents/Artisans' each week.
Some of the 'Local Talents/Artisans' that may be featured will include artists, authors, songwriters and more. The general definition of 'artisan' refers to a worker in a skilled trade, according to the Oxford Dictionary.
Please enjoy Day 23 of the series.
Brady Vice is a singer/songwriter from Fleming County. He has been dabbling in music for quite some time.
'I have been playing music and writing songs for about nine years now,' stated Vice.
Vice said that he enjoys songwriting because it is a way he can participate in 'sharing stories and life experiences through the lens of a song.'
'Certain songs can have many different meanings to many different people,' noted Vice. 'I really enjoy hearing what people say about what I have to share.'
According to Vice, he was apprehensive about sharing his talent with people but no longer is.
'I at first was very nervous to share any of my songs but was fortunate to co-host an open mic at Turtleback Ridge Brewery in Robertson County and that really opened me up. Now I have a feeling of Joy each time I get to write and compose a new song,' explained Vice.
To learn more about Vice and his talent, follow him on Instagram @bradyvice.
'I am currently in the process of recording my debut album with David Austin Tackett at the Bluebank School of Music which should come out sometime this spring or summer. I'll share it there and other places as well,' concluded Vice.

title: Babz Bites: Nan-Nan's Chicken Soup
author: Chef Babz Nartowicz
description: (EDITOR'S NOTE: Please enjoy this encore of a previous column)…
content:
(EDITOR'S NOTE: Please enjoy this encore of a previous column)
The fall weather has a sneakiness about it. One moment it's freezing, the next minute you're peeling off layers of clothing after feeling like you're suffocating.
Growing up, we couldn't wait to throw our backpacks on the sofa after school and peel out of the driveway onto our bicycles. We would ride all over the neighborhood until it was too dark to see the road in front of us. The wind in our hair, dreaming of flying into the wind, it was impossible to not feel the shortness of days and the change in the air, literally. The best part of the adventure would be coming home after a sweaty ride. We would be slightly chilled from the sweat and the temperature change, but mostly starving like we hadn't eaten in days. My grandmother Nan-Nan greeted us with the fragrance of her hot chicken soup cooking wafting from the kitchen. One sip and everything was better. Our body temperature regulated, the warmth flooded through our veins, and suddenly we felt like we could make it.
It was something so subtle but it felt soothing to the bone. Nan-Nan would sometimes just make a simple chicken broth and add rice, or maybe a few vegetables and some noodles. Honestly, like most of her cooking, it was always a little bit different every time. Nan-Nan would use what she had, always making sure to remind us kids that when she was a child they knew how to use every last bit of the chicken. But when she was a kid, people really knew how to cook real food. That was what always separated her soup from anything else, no matter how the recipe changed.
Nan-Nan never used artificial or store bought chicken broth. When we were fighting a bug, or cold, she would simply take some frozen broth out of the freezer, heat it up, and insist we drank up the nourishment.
That broth is consistently a dish I crave whenever I'm under the weather, or honestly just missing my grandmother. Sometimes that is all the motivation I need to make a good pot of soup. It never seems to taste as good as hers, but just like hers it is different every time.
Today's recipe is Nan-Nan's basic chicken soup recipe with a few options for varying the dish.
Good luck and enjoy!
Nan-Nan's Chicken Soup
Feel free to add anything else you love such as potatoes, tomatoes, noodles, squash, zucchini or additional fresh herbs.
1 whole chicken, 3-4 lbs.
6 large carrots, peeled and sliced
6 celery stalks, peeled and sliced (including leaves)
1 vidalia (yellow) onion, diced
5 garlic cloves, diced
Handful of fresh parsley
Handful of fresh dill
2 tsp black peppercorns
3 whole cloves
2 bay leaves (remove after cooking)
Kosher salt (to taste)
Place chicken in a large stock pot or crock pot, and cover with four quarts of water, or cover completely. Add all other ingredients. Heat on medium, or at a boil, if cooking on the stove. Or put a crock pot on high. Skim the top surface for foam, particles, or too much grease. Additional water may need to be added. Cook for about an hour and a half on the stove-top, or 4 hours in the crockpot. Time may vary.
Remove whole chicken as best you can with tongs or two large slotted spoons. Skim the broth again for fat on top. Allow chicken to cool. Once cooled begin deboning, pulling pieces of meat
off into bite sized pieces and placing back into broth. I usually prefer to leave skin out, but that's up to you. Taste broth after adding chicken. It may need additional salt and pepper.
At this time if you would like to add rice, noodles, zucchini, or even saffron or even potatoes. Serve hot. Make plenty.
The recipe and photos used in today's article are from the kitchen of Chef Babz (babzbites@gmail.com) with a little help from her grandmother, Louise Osborne.

title: Polar Bears defeat Black Devils
description: The Bracken County Polar Bears took on the Robertson County Black Devils on the basketball court Thursday night.
content:
The Bracken County Polar Bears took on the Robertson County Black Devils on the basketball court Thursday night.
Both teams entered the contest with a similar record on the season, the Polar Bears sitting at 5-14 on the season, and the Black Devils 4-11. The two teams also have seen each other once prior this season, with the Polar Bears pulling out ahead with a 77-41 victory in the fifth game of the season in December.
When the pair faced off at Robertson County, Bracken County was hoping to pick up another win over the Black Devils, while Robertson County was looking to showcase their growth throughout the season, and defeat one of their most familiar opponents.
The Polar Bears came out strong in the first quarter, outscoring Robertson County 20-12, for an eight point lead heading into the remainder of the first half. Bracken County's Layne Mastin led the team in scoring this quarter, making two threes to total six points at the end of the first eight minutes of play. The Black Devils' Andrew Gooden and Ashton Myers both ended the first quarter with three, Gooden making a three pointer, and Myers one free throw and a field goal.
'We're just trying to run some different offenses. Right now it's about getting prepared for district. We don't know who we're playing, its either gonna be Mason County or Augusta, so right now we're trying to prepare for that. We've got some things to clean up in practice, but other than that we've gotta do better on the defensive end.' said Polar Bears head coach Terry King.
As the first half continued, Bracken County successfully furthered their lead over the Black Devils, outscoring them once again, this time 20-15. Although Robertson County headed into the second half down 40-27, the Black Devils were eager to return to the court, hoping for a late game comeback.
'They're well coached and they play very good defense. We were just trying to get the ball into our big guy. We've been going through him most of the year in Ashton Myers and he's been doing a great job for us. He works hard on both ends and that's what we've been trying to into him so that we could play through him and off of him. That's kinda what we did early on, we just didn't handle the basketball very well or the pressure very well.' said Black Devils head coach, Brandon Hinson.
At the start of the second half, the Polar Bears continued pulling ahead of Robertson County. The Bracken County defense held the Black Devils back to 12 in the third, outscoring them by 15 on the offensive end to head into the fourth quarter leading 67-39. Another strong quarter for the Polar Bears in the fourth would see Bracken County continue to further their lead over the Black Devils, ending the contest up 83-45 over Robertson County.
'We're one of those teams where we've got about six or seven kids who can play. We're in good shape, but that kinda physicalness wears on you over time, over four quarters. We try to go to the bench and play some kids, and those kids work their tails off and work very hard for us but they kinda drop a little bit when we go to our bench. I wasn't disappointed with our bench, coming in with the minutes they gave us, I was disappointed with the glass. I feel like Bracken County just did whatever they wanted on the glass.' said coach Hinson.
Bracken County was proud of their performance, and are continuing to prepare themselves for the upcoming 39th district tournament.
'We played some guys who we normally don't play. Wanted to make sure we get into Saturday and next week healthy also. I wanted to play some guys who normally don't get minutes, to try them out and get them some varsity minutes. Never know who you're gonna need in the district tournament.' said coach King.
Despite the loss, the Black Devils are eager to continue the season and close out their remaining regular season games strong.
'We're frustrated because we believe we're better than what we showed tonight. We believe that we're a little more equal with this team that we played tonight, so we're frustrated because we didn't feel like we gave it our best shot, we felt like we didn't give enough effort on the glass, so we're a little frustrated after that one.' said coach Hinson.

title: Shortest month still a busy one
author: Chuck Hamilton
description: Ah, February.
content:
Ah, February.
As the snow and ice mounds melt away, it's time to look ahead. Not only is February the month of love, but it also signals the end of the NFL season, the beginning of the college baseball season, spring training getting underway for MLB clubs, and high school and college basketball teams preparing for the postseason.
Before we look ahead however, let's take a look in the rearview mirror at what occurred over the weekend.
*****
OL' CHUCK IS WRONG AGAIN – You can't say I haven't warned you in the past. Whenever you see one of my prognostications, take it with a grain of salt. You certainly don't want to wager any hard-earned cash based on my predictions. Another example of my uncanny ability of picking the wrong team to win appeared in my Saturday column. It began with a headline that posed a question, with the eventual answer becoming a resounding 'No.' If you don't already know, the headline read 'Will the Cats flog the Hogs?'
That question was answered rather rudely when former Kentucky coach John Calipari brought his Arkansas team to Rupp Arena and proceeded to thump the Cats 89-79,
ruining the evening for thousands of UK fans watching either in-person or on the idiot box.
It was clear from the outset that the Razorbacks were up to the challenge. Despite coming into the game with a 1-6 record in conference play, Arkansas played like they were the favorite and not a 9.5-point underdog. Calipari and the former Cats now adorned in cardinal and white deserve credit for playing well and earning the victory.
It could be argued that the Hogs played way over their heads in this one, but be that as it may, they outplayed Kentucky in every way imaginable. UK made 10 threes and shot 43.5% from beyond the arc, but Arkansas was better, draining 13-of-25 for 52%. The visitors shot 52% overall, topping the Cats' effort of 48.4%. The Razorbacks outscored the home team in the fast break points category as well by an 18-5 margin. Kentucky continued its woeful free throw shooting as well, making just 9-of-18, while Arkansas sank 12-of-16.
UK did win the rebounding battle 33-30 and outscored the Razorbacks 14-3 in second chance points, but when a bucket was needed to keep the Cats at bay, the Hogs found a way to get it against a defense that has struggled mightily most of the season. Kentucky continues to have a difficult time getting a stop when it is needed the most, and that will likely continue to be an issue.
One reason for the defensive woes is the absence of starting point guard Lamont Butler, whose loss cannot be overstated. Along with being a top-notch defender, Butler makes the offense go with his decision-making. He is also the unquestioned team leader when he's on the floor, and the hope remains that he and his backup, Kerr Kriisa, will return at some point this season. An example of just how much Butler is missed is the Cats have 25 assists and 27 turnovers in their two games without their starting PG. Forward Andrew Carr is still limited due to back issues, but the hope is he can play increased minutes in the near future.
Arkansas was playing shorthanded as well. The team's standout freshman point guard and former UK commit, Boogie Fland, has likely played his last game as a Razorback after suffering a right thumb injury that required UCL surgery. Fland was leading all NCAA freshmen in assist-turnover ratio and in assists per game while averaging 15.1 points per game.
The other Hogs stepped up in a big way in Fland's absence, in particular former UK players Adou Thiero, D.J. Wagner and Zvonimir Ivisic. The chorus of boos and rude treatment from the UK students during warm-ups appeared to inspire the trio as they collectively played their best game of the season.
The hustling Thiero led the way with 21 points and eight rebounds, and he added a few spectacular moves to the basket for good measure. Wagner has assumed the point guard role in place of Fland and looked unguardable, finishing with 17 points and eight assists. Ivisic, despite being overmatched defensively while trying to handle Amari Williams (22 points, 11 boards), added 14 points.
Many Kentucky fans were probably wondering where that was last season. The trio that scored 52 points on Saturday against their former team scored a grand total of five points in their final UK game. That, of course, was the infamous loss to 15-seed Oakland in the first round of the NCAA Tournament last March.
Kentucky can ill afford any more bad losses, which is what the loss to Arkansas was, in more ways than one. But they also have some good wins, and they're still in the hunt for a decent seed in the Big Dance, perhaps a 4 at this point. The Cats have several good wins on their resume, and ample opportunities to tack on a few more. The road does not get any easier however; Kentucky went into Oxford as an underdog against Ole Miss on Tuesday evening after this was written, and they still have games to play against the likes of Tennessee, Texas, Vanderbilt, Alabama, Oklahoma, Auburn and Missouri.
Impatient and demanding UK fans ready to throw in the towel at this juncture need to take a deep breath and hope that head coach Mark Pope can make the necessary adjustments and correct a few of the team's deficiencies as the season winds down. There are several areas in need of improvement to be certain, but hopes of making a deep run in March may hinge on the health of the Cats as much as anything.
*****
EAGLES STILL ON TOP OF OVC – Despite dropping their first home game of the season last Thursday, a 72-64 defeat to Tennessee Tech, the Morehead State Eagles continue to lead the Ohio Valley Conference standings.
MSU is clinging to a one-game advantage in OVC play, with a 9-3 mark, with Little Rock, Southern Illinois-Edwardsville and Southeast Missouri State locked in a three-way tie for second place. The Eagles look to bounce back against SEMO at Johnson Arena on Thursday night.
Sophomore guard Jerone Morton, the George Rogers Clark product, posted a career-high 20 points in the loss to Tennessee Tech.
*****
UK WOMEN CONTINUE TO ROLL – The Kentucky women's basketball team is enjoying a resurgence under first-year head coach Kenny Brooks. The Wildcats
improved to 20-2 on Sunday afternoon with a 95-89 win at Oklahoma.
Georgia Amoore, a 5-foot-6 All-America point guard who came to UK along with Brooks from Virginia Tech, put on a show in Norman. Amoore scored a career-high 43 points, connecting on 15-of-22 from the field, including seven 3-pointers in 12 attempts. She added 6-for-8 from the charity stripe and dished out eight assists. The 43-point performance tied a program high achieved by Jennifer O'Neill in 2013, and matched by Rhyne Howard in 2020.
Clara Strack, another former Hokie, finished with 19 points and the 6-foot-5 sophomore also collected six rebounds, came up with five steals, and blocked a pair of shots. Charlotte transfer Dazia Lawrence, a 5-8 grad student, added 14 points for UK, which is idle until Feb.10 when they travel to Ole Miss.
*****
'Show me a good loser, and I'll show you a loser.' – Red Auerbach
*****
'It was no accident that planted Lincoln on a Kentucky farm, halfway between the lakes and the Gulf. The association there had substance in it. Lincoln belonged just where he was put. If the Union was to be saved, it
had to be a man of such an origin that should save it.' – Mark Twain

content:
Now that the Super Bowl is officially over, we can finally declare it baseball season, although I've personally declared that ever since the Bengals didn't make the playoffs. The sun is shining, warmer days are ahead, and Pitchers & Catchers have officially reported. 'Hey Alexa, play 'The Boys are Back in Town' by Thin Lizzy on high volume.' I am excited to see some sessions from the pitching staff and it's a massive relief to know we have Trevino over Maile this time around as a backup catcher.
Approaching Important Dates
· February 12 – Pitchers and Catchers first workout
· February 15 – Position players report
· February 17 – Full squad workout
· February 22 – First Spring Training Game
· March 27 – Reds Opening Day
Injuries
While the Reds are currently healthy overall, injuries from last year and the offseason will have an impact on this season. Having a relatively healthy Spring is key to beginning the season on a high note. Injuries to Julian Aguiar, Tejay Antone, and Brandon Williamson are notable for now and that list will hopefully remain small, as I don't see any of those players pitching in 2025. Antone possibly could find himself on the mound, but that would require coming back from a third Tommy John surgery.
MLB Pipeline
As we all know, smaller market teams require an influx of young talent year in and year out to remain successful and to compete with billionaire team owners. Included in the Top 100 Prospects this season on the Reds are Chase Burns, Rhett Lowder, Sal Stewart, Cam Collier, and Edwin Arroyo. I believe all of those listed have a chance to make it to the big leagues at some point this season, while we already witnessed what Lowder could do in the majors last season. Fans might just see the Wake Forest duo earlier than expected if Burns is as good as many expect him to be.
Baseball Memories
Everyone who loves the game of baseball in this area has favorite baseball memories, whether that is playing, going to see the Reds, or simply watching them on television with friends or relatives. As baseball season approaches, many of my favorite memories from the past continue to come to my mind. What are some of your favorite baseball memories? Here are a few of mine:
· Chris Reed and Michael Cheesbro took me to my first Reds game, where I recall slipping a note down to Pokey Reese in the dugout, only for him to throw the ball to a fan nearby.
· Attending Opening Day every year with my wife, Jenna. We've created some awesome memories and there is nothing I love more than waking her up at the crack of dawn on the last Thursday of March each year.
· Knothole baseball matchups year after year against Manchester and the battle growing up as a kid. Those were some of the best times.
· Wiffle ball games at Coach Arey's house where a home run was anything hitting the gutter on the house or above, or the tree out in right field. Being a 'town kid' resulted in memories that I will cherish forever roaming from Hopping Avenue and Vine Street to High Street in Peebles.

title: A mishmash of notes for the weekend
author: Chuck Hamilton
description: The goal for this missive is to touch on several topics without going overboard on any of them. If you've read these columns in the past, you know that will not be an easy task for yours truly, so without further ado, let's get this thing started.
content:
The goal for this missive is to touch on several topics without going overboard on any of them. If you've read these columns in the past, you know that will not be an easy task for yours truly, so without further ado, let's get this thing started.
*****
CATS HEAD TO COLUMBIA – The final regular season game of the 2024-25 basketball season for the Kentucky Wildcats will tip at noon today. The Cats are looking to go out on a high note, and continue that momentum into the Southeastern Conference Tournament in Nashville next week, but the homestanding Missouri Tigers are trying to do likewise.
Missouri is favored by 3.5 points because they're always a tough out on their home court in front of their rabid fanbase. The 15th-ranked Tigers are 18-1 in Mizzou Arena, 21-9 overall, and a game in front of UK in the SEC standings at 10-7. They are coming off an unimpressive outing at Oklahoma, and they have dropped three of their last five games, with each of the losses coming on the road. On the other hand, Missouri dealt Alabama a 110-98 setback just two weeks ago in Columbia.
The Cats are hoping to play as well as they did in their final home game, a 95-64 dismantling of a less than mediocre LSU squad on Senior Night in Rupp Arena on Wednesday night. Coach Mark Pope and his team fully realize that Missouri represents a much different breed of Tiger than LSU, and it will take a similar, or an even better performance, to come out of the Show Me State with a victory.
The Tigers feature a ball-hawking defense that leads to transition baskets, so the Cats must be keenly aware of that fact and protect the basketball. Mizzou also has a high-powered offense, led by 6-foot-3 senior guard Caleb Grill, the frontrunner for SEC Sixth Man of the Year. Grill comes off the bench to lead the Tigers in scoring, and is a deadly 3-point shooter. He's tossing in 14.4 points per game and drains 51.1% of his long range attempts at home.
Mark Mitchell, a 6-9 junior, leads Missouri in rebounding and is the second-leading scorer at 14.1 ppg. Tamar Bates, a 6-5 senior, is averaging 13.1 per outing, 6-3 sophomore Anthony Robinson II provides 9.1 ppg, and Iowa transfer Tony Perkins, a 6-4 senior adds 8.1 ppg.
Another name familiar to college basketball followers in this area is 6-3 senior guard Marques Warrick, the all-time scoring leader at Northern Kentucky University, where the southpaw sharpshooter poured in 2,246 points in four seasons. Warrick is playing just 13.7 minutes per game this year and has produced 6.5 points per game, but the Lexington native remains a legitimate threat at the offensive end.
We know the offensive end is also where the Wildcats usually excel, and this one could turn into a shootout. The teams mirror each other in several ways, with the 3-point shot being integral to both offenses.
For underdog Kentucky to pull off the upset, they will need to make their share of shots from beyond the arc, limit the Missouri transition attack, win the rebounding battle, and defend the Tigers efficiently without fouling.
*****
SABO NAMED GRAND MARSHAL – One of my personal all-time favorite Cincinnati Reds was named Friday morning as the 2025 Findlay Market Opening Day Parade Grand Marshal.
Reds Hall of Famer Chris Sabo will be at the forefront of the event, which signals the start of baseball season in the Queen City. It is a well-deserved honor for the likable Sabo, who played a huge part in the winning the 1990 World Series, when the Reds swept the heavily-favored Oakland Athletics. 'Sabes' sizzled at the plate during the Fall Classic, hitting .583 with two home runs and five RBI. In seven seasons with Cincinnati, he hit .270 with 104 home runs, swiped 116 bases, and was named to the All-Star team three times.
Even more so than the stats he put up, the gritty third baseman Sabo endeared himself to Reds fans with his all-out hustling style of play. He was also well-known for wearing goggles during his career after having trouble seeing the ball at night while playing Triple-A baseball. His nickname, Spuds MacKenzie, was given to him by his manager, Pete Rose, during his Rookie of the Year season in 1988. Rose felt that Sabo resembled the popular dog featured in Bud Light commercials at the time.
The parade kicks off at noon on Thursday, March 27 is the just the beginning of all of the festivities that make the day a holiday in Cincinnati, with thousands lining the parade route, and a sold-out crowd attending the Opening Day game against the San Francisco Giants at 4:10 p.m., when 2024 All-Star Hunter Greene takes the mound for the Redlegs.
Reds Hall of Fame and Museum director Rick Walls spoke about Sabo at the announcement.
'He played the game like Pete Rose did and he talks about how he looked up to Pete,' Walls said. 'Pete managed him and I think that it is kind of meaningful this year in the first season we won't have Pete with us.'
*****
SEC DOMINATES COLLEGE BASEBALL – The most recent D1Baseball.com Top 25 has a distinct Southeastern Conference flavor to it, which is par for the course.
The top three teams reside in the SEC, with LSU, defending national champion Tennessee and Arkansas leading the way at 1-2-3. Other SEC schools ranked in the poll include No. 5 Georgia, No. 7 Florida, No. 14 Texas A&M, No. 17 Ole Miss, No. 18 Vanderbilt, No. 22 Auburn and 23rd-ranked Alabama.
Despite opening the season with a 10-1 record, Kentucky is not listed in the D1Baseball rankings. The primary reason for the snub has to be the Bat Cats' thus far unimpressive non-conference schedule. UK is listed as No. 23 in the Baseball America poll, but in that poll, there are 12 SEC teams ranked higher than Kentucky.
It will be interesting to see how this year's rebuilt Bat Cats fare when the competition gets significantly better, but in the early going, they have been firing on all cylinders. They're currently riding a nine-game winning streak; their offensive attack has been explosive, and their pitching has been much better than expected. Kentucky is hitting .290 as a team with 13 home runs and 97 RBI in 11 games, while the team ERA is a minuscule 1.90.
After this weekend's three-game series against Wofford at Kentucky Proud Park, and a home game versus Northern Illinois
on Tuesday, the competition ramps up in a monumental way. UK will open the SEC portion of their schedule at Georgia in a three-game set beginning Friday, March 14. The opening SEC home series is set for March 21-23 against Auburn.
